# RapiDoc

> <rapi-doc> turns an OpenAPI spec into an interactive API reference, as one HTML element with no runtime dependencies.

**RapiDoc** turns an OpenAPI spec into interactive API documentation. At its core is `<rapi-doc>`, a single HTML element with no runtime dependencies: add one script tag and it works in any page or framework. Its Shadow DOM keeps your site's styles and RapiDoc's styles apart.

<CardGrid>
  <LinkCard title="Quickstart" description="An API reference in one HTML file." href="/docs/rapidoc/get-started/quickstart/" />
  <LinkCard title="Which package do I need?" description="Every package in the RapiDoc family and when you need it." href="/docs/#which-package-do-i-need" />
</CardGrid>

## What you can build

<CardGrid>
  <DocsCard title="API reference" icon="book-open">
    `<rapi-doc>` renders navigation, search, schemas, examples, authentication and a **Try** console. Choose one long page, expandable sections, or one operation at a time. [Quickstart](/docs/rapidoc/get-started/quickstart/)
  </DocsCard>
  <DocsCard title="Your look" icon="pencil-simple">
    Six built-in themes, any brand color, light and dark, and full control through CSS custom properties and `::part()`. [Theming](/docs/rapidoc/theming/overview/)
  </DocsCard>
  <DocsCard title="A mock in the page" icon="hard-drives">
    Answer **Try** from the spec's examples and schemas, with nothing to deploy. [In-browser mock](/docs/rapidoc/mocking/in-browser/)
  </DocsCard>
  <DocsCard title="Tools for AI agents" icon="robot">
    A button in `<rapi-doc>` turns the spec into a curated MCP server. [Export MCP Server](/docs/rapidoc/mcp-export/)
  </DocsCard>
</CardGrid>

## The rest of the family

`<rapi-doc>` is one of several products: RapiDoc Mini, RapiFlow, RapiPdf, RapiMock and RapiDoc Portal, with the RapiDoc CLI, MCP and pre-rendering as tools. The [documentation home](/docs/) lists them all.

Every attribute, method, event and slot of `<rapi-doc>` is listed in the [API reference](/docs/rapidoc/reference/), and the [Examples](/examples) show it running.

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/rapidoc/

---

# Authentication

> How readers give <rapi-doc> the credentials Try needs to call a protected API - API keys, HTTP Basic, bearer tokens and OAuth 2.0 - and how your page can fill them in.

When an API needs credentials, **Try** has to send them. `<rapi-doc>` reads the security schemes your spec declares (`components.securitySchemes`) and shows an **Authentication** section with a form for each: the reader enters a key, a token, a username and password, or signs in with your identity provider. Every **Try** request to an operation that uses that scheme then carries the credential.

The credentials stay in the reader's browser and go only to your API. They are forgotten on reload unless you set [`persist-auth`](#keep-them-across-reloads).

## What each scheme asks for

| Scheme in the spec | The reader enters | Your page can fill it in with |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `apiKey` (header, query or cookie) | The key | `setApiKey('schemeId', key)` |
| `http` with `scheme: basic` | Username and password | `setHttpUserNameAndPassword('schemeId', user, password)` |
| `http` with `scheme: bearer` | The token (RapiDoc adds `Bearer `) | `setApiKey('schemeId', token)` |
| `oauth2`, `openIdConnect` | Signs in with your provider, in a popup | `setApiKey('schemeId', accessToken)`, with a token you already have |

`schemeId` is the scheme's name under `components.securitySchemes`. OAuth sign-in needs a small receiver page and a client registered with your provider: [OAuth 2.0](/docs/rapidoc/authentication/oauth/) sets it up in three steps.

## Fill them in from your page

When your site already knows who the reader is, pass their credential to `<rapi-doc>` so they don't have to paste it. Add a `note` and the Authentication section shows it in place of the form, with a link to use a different token:

```js
const doc = document.querySelector('rapi-doc');
doc.setApiKey('BearerAuth', sessionToken, { note: 'Using your sign-in (ann@example.com).' });
```

`removeAllSecurityKeys()` clears every credential, for example when the reader signs out. All the methods are on the [Methods](/docs/rapidoc/reference/methods/) reference page.

## An API key the spec doesn't declare

If the spec has no security scheme for it, set the key with attributes, and it is sent with every **Try** request:

```html
<rapi-doc
  spec-url="https://rapidocui.com/specs/petstore.yaml"
  api-key-name="X-API-Key"
  api-key-location="header"
  api-key-value="test-key-123"
></rapi-doc>
```

## Keep them across reloads

`persist-auth="true"` keeps API keys, bearer tokens and OAuth access tokens in the browser's `localStorage`, so a reload doesn't sign the reader out. An OAuth token is dropped once it expires; HTTP Basic credentials and OAuth client secrets are never stored.

## Hide the forms

`allow-authentication="false"` hides the Authentication section, for a page that fills in every credential itself or an API that needs none.

> **Caution: Calls from the browser**
> **Try** calls your API from the reader's browser, so the API must allow cross-origin requests from your docs site, including the `Authorization` header (or your API key's header) in `Access-Control-Allow-Headers`.

## Sign-in for the docs themselves

This page is about signing in to **your API**, so **Try** works. To put the **documentation** behind a sign-in (Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google or any OpenID Connect provider), with rules for who may read which pages, use [RapiDoc Portal's single sign-on](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/access/overview/).

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/rapidoc/authentication/

---

# OAuth 2.0

> Let readers sign in with your OAuth 2.0 or OpenID Connect provider and call your API from RapiDoc, using <oauth-receiver> and vendor extensions.

When a spec declares an OAuth 2.0 security scheme, RapiDoc's Authentication section lets readers sign in with your identity provider (Okta, Auth0, Microsoft Entra ID, Keycloak and others). The access token is then sent with every **Try** request.

> **Tip:**
> Try it on the [OAuth 2.0 example](/examples/oauth-demo). It signs in at Duende's public demo provider, `demo.duendesoftware.com`, which anyone can use for testing: client `interactive.public` (PKCE, no secret), or `interactive.confidential.short` with the secret `secret`.

## Set it up in three steps

1. **Register a client** with your identity provider, and add your receiver page as a redirect URI, for example `https://docs.example.com/oauth-receiver.html`. Make it a single-page application (a public client) with the Authorization Code grant and PKCE, and allow your docs site's origin, so the browser can call the token endpoint.
2. **Declare the scheme in your spec** (below), and show the spec with `<rapi-doc>` as usual.
3. **Add `oauth-receiver.html`** next to the page with `<rapi-doc>`:

   ```html title="oauth-receiver.html"
   <!doctype html>
   <html lang="en">
     <head>
       <meta charset="utf-8" />
       <script type="module" src="https://unpkg.com/rapidoc/dist/rapidoc-min.js"></script>
     </head>
     <body>
       <oauth-receiver></oauth-receiver>
     </body>
   </html>
   ```

If the receiver page lives elsewhere, tell `<rapi-doc>` where:

```html
<rapi-doc spec-url="/openapi.json" oauth-receiver="/auth/oauth-receiver.html"></rapi-doc>
```

## How sign-in works

1. The reader clicks **Authorize** in the Authentication section.
2. `<rapi-doc>` builds the authorization URL (client ID, scopes, `redirect_uri` set to your receiver page, `state`, a nonce and, with PKCE, a code challenge) and opens it in a popup.
3. The reader signs in at the provider, which redirects the popup to `oauth-receiver.html?code=…&state=…`.
4. `<oauth-receiver>` removes the code from the popup's URL and hands it to the opening page, through `window.opener` and a `BroadcastChannel`.
5. `<rapi-doc>` checks `state`, closes the popup and exchanges the code for a token at the provider's token endpoint.
6. The token is kept in memory (never in `localStorage`) and sent with every **Try** request, using the token type from the provider's response (normally `Bearer`).

PKCE (S256) is on by default and can be turned off in the form, unless the scheme sets `x-pkce-only: true`. The implicit flow is supported too: `<oauth-receiver>` reads the token from the URL fragment.

To try it locally, serve the folder over HTTP (`npx serve`, Vite or any static server): a provider can't redirect to a `file://` page. After signing in, the scheme shows as authorized and **Try** sends the token.

## Declare the scheme

Use a standard OpenAPI `oauth2` security scheme:

```yaml
components:
  securitySchemes:
    OAuth:
      type: oauth2
      flows:
        authorizationCode:
          authorizationUrl: https://auth.example.com/oauth2/authorize
          tokenUrl: https://auth.example.com/oauth2/token
          scopes:
            read:profile: Read your profile
            write:profile: Change your profile

paths:
  /user/profile:
    get:
      summary: Get the current user's profile
      security:
        - OAuth: [read:profile]
```

## Vendor extensions

These extensions pre-fill the sign-in form, which is useful for sandboxes and public clients. `x-pkce-only` goes on the flow; the others work on the flow or on the scheme (the flow wins).

| Extension | Type | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `x-client-id` | `string` | Pre-fills the client ID. |
| `x-client-secret` | `string` | Pre-fills the client secret. For sandboxes only: anyone can read the spec. |
| `x-default-scopes` | `string` or `array` | Scopes selected by default: a space-separated string or a list. |
| `x-pkce-only` | `boolean` | Always uses PKCE and hides the client secret fields. Use it for public clients. |
| `x-receive-token-in` | `request-body` or `header` | How the client credentials are sent to the token endpoint: in the body (`client_secret_post`, the default) or as HTTP Basic (`client_secret_basic`). |
| `x-receive-token-in-options` | `array` | Limits the choices offered for the above. |
| `x-authorize-params` | `object` or `string` | Extra query parameters for the authorization URL, such as `prompt` or `audience`. |
| `x-token-params` | `object` or `string` | Extra parameters for the token request, such as `audience` or `resource`. |

```yaml
components:
  securitySchemes:
    # A public client: PKCE only, no secret
    public-oauth:
      type: oauth2
      flows:
        authorizationCode:
          authorizationUrl: https://demo.duendesoftware.com/connect/authorize
          tokenUrl: https://demo.duendesoftware.com/connect/token
          scopes:
            openid: OpenID Connect
            profile: Your profile
          x-client-id: interactive.public
          x-default-scopes: [openid, profile]
          x-pkce-only: true
          x-authorize-params:
            prompt: consent
          x-token-params:
            audience: https://api.example.com

    # A sandbox client with a pre-filled test secret
    sandbox-oauth:
      type: oauth2
      x-client-id: interactive.confidential.short
      x-client-secret: secret
      x-default-scopes: openid email
      flows:
        authorizationCode:
          authorizationUrl: https://demo.duendesoftware.com/connect/authorize
          tokenUrl: https://demo.duendesoftware.com/connect/token
          scopes:
            openid: OpenID Connect
            email: Your email address
```

## Extra parameters for the provider

Some providers and proxies need extra parameters, such as `audience`, `resource`, or a SMART on FHIR `launch` value. Besides the `x-authorize-params` and `x-token-params` extensions, you can set them on the element.

### As attributes

Both attributes take JSON or a URL query string:

```html
<rapi-doc
  spec-url="/openapi.json"
  additional-authorize-params='{"launch": "xyz123", "prompt": "consent"}'
  additional-token-params="audience=https%3A%2F%2Fapi.example.com"
></rapi-doc>
```

Or set objects on the properties: `doc.additionalAuthorizeParams = { launch: 'xyz123' }`.

### From JavaScript

Two events let you change the requests as they are made. Both can be cancelled with `e.preventDefault()`.

```javascript
const doc = document.querySelector('rapi-doc');

// Before the popup opens; authParams is a live URLSearchParams
doc.addEventListener('before-authorize', (e) => {
  const { securitySchemeId, flowType, authUrl, authParams } = e.detail;
  authParams.set('launch', sessionStorage.getItem('launch') || 'test-launch');
});

// Before the token request; params (body) is a URLSearchParams, headers is a Headers
doc.addEventListener('before-token-request', (e) => {
  const { securitySchemeId, grantType, tokenUrl, params, headers } = e.detail;
  params.set('resource', 'https://api.example.com');
});
```

## Troubleshooting

- **Redirect URI mismatch**: the redirect URI registered with the provider must match the receiver page's URL exactly, including protocol and port (for example `http://localhost:4321/oauth-receiver.html`).
- **CORS on the token endpoint**: the browser calls the token endpoint directly, so it must allow requests from your docs site's origin.
- **Client authentication**: if the provider requires HTTP Basic for client credentials, set `x-receive-token-in: header`, or pick it in the form.
- **"Multiple client credentials cannot be specified"**: the provider received the client in the request body and in an `Authorization` header (RFC 6749 §2.3.1 allows only one). RapiDoc sends one or the other, and with no secret only `client_id` and the PKCE `code_verifier`, so check for a proxy or gateway that adds a header.
- **The popup doesn't open**: browsers block popups that a click didn't open. Sign in from the **Authorize** button, not from a script.
- **The receiver page isn't found**: the file name is case-sensitive on most servers; `oauth-receiver.html` must match the `oauth-receiver` attribute and the registered redirect URI.
- **Secrets**: never put a production client secret in a spec. Use `x-pkce-only: true` for public docs and keep `x-client-secret` for sandboxes.

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/rapidoc/authentication/oauth/

---

# Links & Navigation

> Element IDs, links between operations in Markdown descriptions, tag groups, URL routing and navigating from JavaScript.

Every section, tag and operation in `<rapi-doc>` has a stable element ID. You can link to these IDs from Markdown descriptions in your spec, from your own page, or from JavaScript.

> **Tip:**
> The [Links example](/examples/links) shows these links working, using [`links.yaml`](/specs/links.yaml).

## Element IDs

| Target | ID | Example |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Overview | `overview` | |
| API Servers | `servers` | |
| Authentication | `auth` | |
| Tag | `tag--` + tag name in kebab-case | `User Management & Auth` → `tag--user-management-auth` |
| Tag group (`x-tagGroups`, or a 3.2 parent tag) | `tag-group--` + group or parent tag name in kebab-case | `Shipment Logistics` → `tag-group--shipment-logistics` |
| Operation | see below | `getUserById` → `get-user-by-id` |
| Heading in a description | see [Markdown Headings](/docs/rapidoc/customizing/markdown-headings/#links-to-headings) | `overview--authentication` |

IDs are lowercase and case-sensitive: `#tag--users` works, `#tag--Users` does not.

### Operation IDs

An operation's ID comes from the first of these that applies:

1. **`operationId`** in kebab-case, if it is at most 45 characters and not a placeholder such as `operation1`: `getUserById` → `get-user-by-id`.
2. **`summary`** in kebab-case, cut at a word boundary after 40 characters: `Get a user by ID` → `get-a-user-by-id`.
3. **Method and path**: `GET /users/{userId}` → `get-users-userid`.

If two operations would get the same ID, the second gets its method in front (`post-webhooks`), then a number. With `x-tagGroups`, every operation ID starts with its tag: `users--get-user-by-id`. Groups made from OpenAPI 3.2 `parent` tags don't add that prefix.

An ID made from the summary changes whenever the summary is edited, so give operations an `operationId` when links to them should last. `rapidoc lint` reports operations without one.

Every operation can also be reached by its **method and path**, whatever its ID: `#get-users-userid`, or `#delete-orgs-orgid-teams-teamid` for `DELETE /orgs/{orgId}/teams/{teamId}`. Case and punctuation are ignored there, so links in the format of older RapiDoc versions (`#get-/users/{userId}`) keep working.

## Links in descriptions

Markdown links to an ID work in any description in the spec: `info.description`, tags, operations, parameters and responses. Clicking one scrolls to the target, opening its tag and operation if they are collapsed, in every render mode.

```yaml
paths:
  /users:
    post:
      operationId: createUser
      summary: Create a user
      description: |
        Read the new user back with [Get a user](#get-user-by-id).
        You need a token first; see [Authentication](#auth).
  /users/{userId}:
    get:
      operationId: getUserById
      summary: Get a user
      description: To add a user, use [Create a user](#create-user).
```

## Tag groups

For APIs with many tags, the `x-tagGroups` extension (also spelled `x-tag-groups`) adds a level above tags in the sidebar and the content:

```yaml
x-tagGroups:
  - name: Shipments
    tags: [Shipments, Tracking, Rates]
  - name: Billing
    x-tag-expanded: false   # starts collapsed
    tags: [Invoices, Payments]
```

Clicking a tag or group in the sidebar opens or closes it. A group starts expanded unless it has `x-tag-expanded: false` (`x-tagExpanded`, `x-expanded` and `expanded` work too).

### OpenAPI 3.2 parent tags

OpenAPI 3.2 has its own way to nest tags: `parent` on a tag names the tag it belongs under. RapiDoc shows it the same way as `x-tagGroups`, with the parent's `summary` as the group's heading:

```yaml
openapi: 3.2.0
tags:
  - name: shop
    summary: Shop
    description: Pets and the orders placed for them
  - name: pet
    summary: Pets
    parent: shop
  - name: store
    summary: Store
    parent: shop
```

- A tag's `summary` is its name in the sidebar and headings (`x-displayName` still wins when both are set).
- A parent tag with no operations of its own is only the group's heading. One with operations comes first in its group.
- RapiDoc nests one level: a tag whose parent has a parent of its own goes in the top-level tag's group.
- Operation IDs keep no tag prefix, unlike with `x-tagGroups`.
- When a spec has both, `x-tagGroups` decides the groups.
- Tags with a `kind` other than `nav` (`badge`, `audience`) are not sections: an operation is listed under its navigation tags, and a `kind: badge` tag is shown as a badge on it.

## The address bar

| Attribute | Default | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `update-route` | `true` | Puts the ID of the section in view into the URL hash, so readers can bookmark and share it. |
| `goto-path` | | An ID to scroll to once the spec has loaded, when the URL has no hash. |
| `scroll-behavior` | `smooth` | `smooth` or `auto` (jump). |

Opening a URL with a hash scrolls to that ID.

### In a single-page app

When your app's router owns the URL, set `update-route="false"` and follow RapiDoc's position through the `nav-active-change` event. Its `detail` is `{ id, elementId }`.

```javascript
const doc = document.querySelector('rapi-doc');
doc.addEventListener('nav-active-change', (e) => {
  router.replace({ hash: `#${e.detail.elementId}` });
});
```

RapiDoc updates the URL with `history.replaceState`, which doesn't fire `hashchange`, so listen for `nav-active-change` rather than `hashchange`.

## Navigating from JavaScript

```javascript
const doc = document.querySelector('rapi-doc');

doc.scrollToPath('get-user-by-id');       // an operation, by ID or method and path
doc.scrollToPath('get-/users/{userId}');  // the older format works too
doc.scrollToPath('tag--users');           // a tag
doc.scrollToPath('servers');              // a section
```

Links in your own HTML, such as `<a href="#get-user-by-id">` in your page, work through the URL hash. To place links inside `<rapi-doc>`, use [slots](/docs/rapidoc/customizing/slots/).

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/rapidoc/customizing/linking/

---

# Markdown Headings in the Sidebar

> Turn the

Many specs carry real documentation in their descriptions: a getting-started section, authentication, rate limits. With `info-description-headings-in-navbar="true"`, RapiDoc lists the level-1 (`#`) and level-2 (`##`) headings of those descriptions in the sidebar, so readers can jump to them.

> **Tip:**
> See it on the [Markdown Headings example](/examples/markdown-headings), which uses [`markdown-headings.yaml`](/specs/markdown-headings.yaml).

## Set it up

1. Turn it on, in `read` or `focused` mode (`view` mode has no sidebar):

   ```html
   <rapi-doc
     spec-url="/specs/markdown-headings.yaml"
     render-style="read"
     info-description-headings-in-navbar="true"
   ></rapi-doc>
   ```

2. Write headings in `info.description` or in a tag's `description`:

   ```yaml
   info:
     title: Fleet Management API
     version: 1.0.0
     description: |
       # Getting Started
       Welcome to the Fleet API.

       ## Authentication
       Every request needs an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.

       ### Token lifetime
       Level-3 headings stay in the text and don't appear in the sidebar.

   tags:
     - name: Vehicles
       description: |
         Manage connected vehicles.

         # The Vehicle Object
         Fields and their meaning.
   ```

Headings from `info.description` appear under the overview item at the top of the sidebar (labeled with `info.title`). Headings from a tag's description appear under that tag. Headings in operation descriptions are not listed.

## Links to headings

Each heading gets an ID you can link to, made from its text with the same rules GitHub uses for heading anchors:

| Heading | ID |
| :--- | :--- |
| `## Authentication` in `info.description` | `overview--authentication` |
| `## Rate Limits & Quotas` in `info.description` | `overview--rate-limits--quotas` |
| `# The Vehicle Object` under the tag `Vehicles` | `tag--vehicles--the-vehicle-object` |

IDs are case-sensitive. Clicking a heading in the sidebar scrolls to it and, with `update-route="true"` (the default), puts its ID in the address bar.

## Styling

Heading items under tags have the parts `section-navbar-h1` and `section-navbar-h2`; the overview item has `section-navbar-overview`. Headings under the overview item have no part of their own: style them through the CSS variables on [Styling with CSS](/docs/rapidoc/theming/css-parts/).

```css
rapi-doc::part(section-navbar-h1) {
  font-weight: 600;
}
rapi-doc::part(section-navbar-h2) {
  padding-left: 24px;
}
```

## Headings don't show up?

- `info-description-headings-in-navbar="true"` is on the element, and `render-style` is `read` or `focused`.
- The heading is `#` or `##` followed by a space (`# Introduction`, not `#Introduction`).
- It is in `info.description` or a tag's `description`.
- For overview headings, the overview is shown: `show-info` is not `false`.

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/rapidoc/customizing/markdown-headings/

---

# Your Own Markup

> Put your own HTML, such as a logo, banners, notices and a footer, inside <rapi-doc> with named slots.

`<rapi-doc>` renders inside a Shadow DOM, so you can't insert elements into it directly. Instead it has **slots**: named places where your own HTML appears. Put an element inside `<rapi-doc>` and give it a `slot` attribute naming the place; children without a `slot` go to the default slot. Slotted elements stay in your page's DOM, so your page's CSS styles them.

```html
<rapi-doc spec-url="https://rapidocui.com/specs/petstore.yaml" show-header="true">
  <img slot="logo" src="/brand/logo.svg" alt="Acme" height="28" />

  <a slot="header" href="https://github.com/acme/api">GitHub</a>

  <div class="banner">Welcome to the Acme API v2.4. Read the new authentication guide.</div>

  <p slot="auth">Need a key? Create one in the <a href="https://console.acme.com">developer console</a>.</p>

  <footer slot="footer">© 2026 Acme Corp. <a href="/terms">Terms</a></footer>
</rapi-doc>
```

> **Tip:**
> The [Slots example](/examples/slots) lets you try every slot.

## Every slot

The [reference](/docs/rapidoc/reference/slots/) lists every slot and where it appears. Two kinds are made from the spec: `tag--<tag id>` under a tag's heading, and `<operation id>` inside one operation, both in `read` and `view` modes.

## Tag and operation slots

Tag and operation slots are named after the element IDs RapiDoc gives them, so they follow the same rules as links (see [Links & Navigation](/docs/rapidoc/customizing/linking/#element-ids)):

- **Tags**: `tag--` and the tag name in lowercase kebab-case. The tag `Pet` is `tag--pet`; `User Management` is `tag--user-management`.
- **Operations**: the `operationId` in kebab-case (`getPetById` is `get-pet-by-id`); without one, the summary or the method and path.

```html
<rapi-doc spec-url="https://rapidocui.com/specs/petstore.yaml">
  <div slot="tag--pet">Pet IDs are 64-bit integers.</div>
  <div slot="get-pet-by-id">Responses from this endpoint are cached for 60 seconds.</div>
</rapi-doc>
```

When the spec uses `x-tagGroups`, an operation's ID starts with its tag (`pet--get-pet-by-id`). If a slot doesn't show up, find the ID in the page's address bar after clicking the operation, or in the browser's element inspector.

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/rapidoc/customizing/slots/

---

# Loading Your Spec

> Which OpenAPI versions RapiDoc reads, the three ways to give it a spec, and how to handle CORS.

## Supported versions

| Version | Support |
| :--- | :--- |
| **OpenAPI 3.1** and **3.2** | Read as they are, including JSON Schema 2020-12 and `webhooks`. |
| **OpenAPI 3.0** | Read as it is. |
| **Swagger 2.0** | Upgraded to OpenAPI 3.1 in the browser before rendering. For large specs, convert ahead of time (see [Large Specs](/docs/rapidoc/performance/large-specs/)). |

Specs can be JSON or YAML. RapiDoc resolves `$ref`s, including references to other files relative to the spec's URL, but does not validate the spec: use [`rapidoc validate`](/docs/cli/validate/) for that.

## Three ways to load a spec

### From a URL

```html
<rapi-doc spec-url="https://api.example.com/v1/openapi.yaml"></rapi-doc>
```

Changing `spec-url` later loads the new spec.

> **Caution: Specs on another domain**
> The browser fetches the spec, so a spec on a different domain or port than the page must be served with CORS headers, at least:
>
>   ```http
>   Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *
>   ```
>
>   If you can't change that server, serve a copy of the spec from your own site, or fetch it yourself and use `loadSpec`.

### From JavaScript

`loadSpec()` takes a spec object or a URL. Use it when you fetch the spec yourself, for example with the user's credentials:

```javascript
const doc = document.querySelector('rapi-doc');

const res = await fetch('/internal/openapi.json', {
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${sessionToken}` },
});
doc.loadSpec(await res.json());
```

### Inside the element

Put the spec as JSON in a `<script>` inside `<rapi-doc>`, with `slot="rapidoc-spec"`. It is read once, when the element is added to the page, and takes precedence over `spec-url`.

```html
<rapi-doc>
  <script type="application/json" slot="rapidoc-spec">
    {
      "openapi": "3.1.0",
      "info": { "title": "Embedded API", "version": "1.0.0" },
      "paths": {}
    }
  </script>
</rapi-doc>
```

## How OpenAPI features are shown

- **`oneOf` and `anyOf`**: the variants are listed as numbered options (OPT 1, OPT 2, …) under a ONE OF or ANY OF label. `allOf` is merged into one schema.
- **Several examples**: when a media type has an `examples` map, a picker switches between them.
- **Servers and server variables**: the API Servers section lists the spec's `servers`; readers pick one, and fill in its variables (such as `{environment}`), before pressing **Try**.

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/rapidoc/get-started/openapi-support/

---

# Quickstart

> Show an interactive API reference for your OpenAPI spec in one HTML file.

Build one HTML file that shows RapiDoc's interactive reference for an OpenAPI spec. You need a browser and an internet connection. To use a spec file from your computer in step 3, you also need a local web server, such as `npx serve`, which needs Node.js.

<Steps>

1. **Create an HTML file** that loads RapiDoc and points `<rapi-doc>` at the sample Petstore spec:

   ```html title="index.html"
   <!doctype html>
   <html lang="en">
     <head>
       <meta charset="utf-8" />
       <script type="module" src="https://unpkg.com/rapidoc/dist/rapidoc-min.js"></script>
       <style>
         rapi-doc { height: 100vh; }
       </style>
     </head>
     <body>
       <rapi-doc spec-url="https://rapidocui.com/specs/petstore.yaml"></rapi-doc>
     </body>
   </html>
   ```

2. **Open it in a browser.** You get navigation, search, schemas and a **Try** console that sends requests to the Petstore's public server, `petstore3.swagger.io`.

3. **Point `spec-url` at your own spec**, an OpenAPI 3.x or Swagger 2.0 file in JSON or YAML, and reload: your API's operations replace the Petstore's. For a spec on a server, use its URL. For a file, put it next to `index.html`, run `npx serve` in that folder, open the address it prints and set `spec-url="openapi.yaml"` (your file's name).

</Steps>

> **Tip: Sizing**
> `<rapi-doc>` fills the height you give it. Set a height (here `100vh`) and keep its default `display: flex`: with `display: block` the bottom of the content is cut off.

For production, pin a major version (`https://unpkg.com/rapidoc@14/dist/rapidoc-min.js`), so a new major version can't change attributes under you, or serve the file from your own site.

## Troubleshooting

| What you see | What to do |
| :--- | :--- |
| A spec on another domain doesn't load | That server must allow cross-origin requests: see [Loading Your Spec](/docs/rapidoc/get-started/openapi-support/#from-a-url). |
| A spec file next to the page doesn't load | Browsers block a page opened from disk (`file://`) from reading other files. Run `npx serve` in the folder, open the address it prints, and use `spec-url="openapi.yaml"` (your file's name). |
| **Try** fails with a network error | Your API must allow cross-origin requests from the page, including the `Authorization` header (or your API key's header). |

## Install from npm

With a bundler, install the package and import it once in your entry file. The import registers `<rapi-doc>`; use it in your markup as above. With server rendering (Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit), import it in the browser only. See [Front-End Frameworks](/docs/integrations/front-end/).

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="npm">
    ```bash frame="terminal" title="terminal"
    npm install rapidoc
    ```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="pnpm">
    ```bash frame="terminal" title="terminal"
    pnpm add rapidoc
    ```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="yarn">
    ```bash frame="terminal" title="terminal"
    yarn add rapidoc
    ```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

```javascript
import 'rapidoc';
```

## Without a CDN

To serve everything yourself, on an intranet or an air-gapped network, copy the bundle out of the npm package. RapiDoc then loads nothing from a third-party host; requests go to your spec's URL and the servers it names.

In `index.html`, set the script's `src` to `rapidoc-min.js` and `spec-url` to `openapi.yaml`. Then put the page, your spec and the bundle in one folder, here `public/`:

```bash frame="terminal" title="terminal"
npm install rapidoc
mkdir -p public
cp node_modules/rapidoc/dist/rapidoc-min.js* public/   # the bundle and its license notices
cp index.html openapi.yaml public/                     # your page and your spec
```

Any web server can serve the folder; in a container:

```dockerfile title="Dockerfile"
FROM nginx:alpine
COPY public/ /usr/share/nginx/html/
```

# Export MCP Server

> The Export MCP Server button of <rapi-doc> and its JavaScript methods, which turn the spec on the page into an MCP server project for AI agents.

`<rapi-doc>` can turn the spec it shows into an MCP server for AI agents, in the browser: nothing is sent to a server. How operations become tools, the manifest and the project it downloads are on [MCP Server](/docs/mcp/), with [Export and run the server](/docs/mcp/server/) for running it and connecting an AI app.

## The button

Set the `mcp` attribute:

```html
<rapi-doc
  spec-url="/specs/my-api.yaml"
  mcp="true"
  mcp-server-name="my-api"
> </rapi-doc>
```

- **`mcp`** (default `"false"`): `"true"` shows an **Export MCP Server** button in the API overview that downloads the project as a zip. `"false"`, `"none"` or an empty value hides it.
- **`mcp-server-name`** (optional): the server's name. Defaults to the spec's title. It is only a name, not a running service: it becomes the download's name (`my-api-mcp.zip`), the package name (`my-api`) and the key of the `mcpServers` entry (`my_api`).

## From JavaScript

You can build the manifest, trigger the download, or check the token budget from code. Every method accepts an `options` object with `serverName`, `includeInternal`, `includeDeprecated` and `includeOperations` (`false` keeps only the workflow tools):

```javascript
const doc = document.querySelector('rapi-doc');

// 1. Build the manifest, the project files and the token diagnostics in memory
const result = doc.generateMcpServer({ serverName: 'my-api' });
console.log(result.manifest.tools.map((t) => t.name)); // ['place_order', 'get_order', ...]
console.log(result.files['server.ts']);                 // every file of the zip, path → text
console.log(result.budget);                             // { totalTools: 5, estimatedTokens: 850, ... }
console.log(result.hostConfig);                         // the text of mcp.json

// 2. Download the project as <server-name>-mcp.zip
doc.downloadMcpServer();

// 3. Inspect token budget overhead before exporting
const budget = doc.getMcpBudget();
console.log(`Overhead: ~${budget.estimatedTokens} tokens/turn across ${budget.totalTools} tools.`);
```

`result.files` has the keys `manifest.json`, `server.ts`, `runtime.js`, `package.json`, `README.md` and `mcp.json`, plus `workflow-runtime.js` when there are workflows. `getMcpBudget()` returns `{ totalTools, totalResources, estimatedTokens, consequentialCount, warnings }`, where `consequentialCount` is the number of tools that are not read-only.

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/rapidoc/mcp-export/

---

# Migrating from RapiDoc v10 to v11

> Upgrade guide for migrating from RapiDoc v10 to v11. Learn about deprecated styling attributes, modern CSS custom properties (design tokens), and W3C CSS Shadow Parts (::part()).

> **Note: Upgrading to v12?**
> v12 renamed several of the CSS variables this guide introduces. Follow this guide first, then [v11 to v12](/docs/rapidoc/migration/v11-to-v12/).

RapiDoc **v11** introduces a modernized styling architecture designed around **W3C web standards**, **CSS custom properties (design tokens)**, and **CSS Shadow Parts (`::part()`)**.

This major release eliminates attribute bloat by deprecating granular styling attributes (`bg-color`, `text-color`, `nav-bg-color`, `primary-color`, `regular-font`, etc.) in favor of standard CSS declarations and high-level design tokens.

> **Tip: Why the Styling Architecture Changed**
> In RapiDoc v10, customizing visuals required configuring dozens of specialized HTML attributes. While functional, this approach:
>   - Cluttered HTML templates with styling configuration.
>   - Failed to integrate cleanly with modern design systems (Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, CSS variables).
>   - Lacked native CSS cascade and media query support (such as automatic `prefers-color-scheme` detection).
>   - Could not leverage rich CSS capabilities like gradients, backdrop blur, transitions, and hover states.
>
> **RapiDoc v11** standardizes styling into **high-level declarative tokens** on the element itself, and **CSS variables & `::part()` pseudo-elements** for all visual customizations.

---

## 1. Quick Summary of Breaking Changes

Here is an overview of what changed between v10 and v11:

1. **`theme` attribute redefined**:
   - **v10**: Used for base mode (`theme="dark"` or `theme="light"`).
   - **v11**: Sets the **color palette preset** (`amber`, `blue`, `emerald`, `violet`, `graphite`, `rose`, `slate`) OR accepts any custom brand hex code (`theme="#2563eb"`).
2. **`color-scheme` attribute introduced**:
   - Controls light/dark surface rendering: `color-scheme="dark"`, `color-scheme="light"`, or `color-scheme="system"`.
3. **Granular color attributes deprecated**:
   - `bg-color`, `text-color`, `header-color`, `primary-color` are replaced by the `theme` preset engine, `--background`, `--foreground`, `--primary`, or `::part()`.
4. **Navigation color attributes deprecated**:
   - `nav-bg-color`, `nav-text-color`, `nav-hover-bg-color`, `nav-hover-text-color`, `nav-accent-color`, `nav-accent-text-color` are replaced by CSS custom properties and `rapi-doc::part(section-navbar)`.
5. **Font attributes deprecated**:
   - `regular-font` and `mono-font` are replaced by standard CSS variables `--font-sans` and `--font-mono`.
   - `font-size="default | large | largest"` is replaced by proportional UI scaling attribute `scale="sm | default | lg"`.

---

## 2. Deprecated Attributes & Modern Replacements

The table below maps every deprecated v10 attribute to its modern v11 replacement:

| Legacy v10 Attribute             |                    Status                    | Modern v11 Replacement                                           | Type / Mechanism              |
| :------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------: | :--------------------------------------------------------------- | :---------------------------- |
| `theme="light"` / `theme="dark"` | <Badge text="Deprecated" variant="danger" /> | `color-scheme`                                                   | HTML Attribute                |
| `primary-color`                  | <Badge text="Deprecated" variant="danger" /> | `theme` or `--primary`                                           | HTML Attribute / CSS Variable |
| `bg-color`                       | <Badge text="Deprecated" variant="danger" /> | `--background` or `color-scheme`                                 | CSS Variable / HTML Attribute |
| `text-color`                     | <Badge text="Deprecated" variant="danger" /> | `--foreground`                                                   | CSS Variable                  |
| `header-color`                   | <Badge text="Deprecated" variant="danger" /> | `::part(section-header)` or `--header-bg`                        | CSS Shadow Part / Variable    |
| `regular-font`                   | <Badge text="Deprecated" variant="danger" /> | `--font-sans` (or `--font-regular`)                              | CSS Variable                  |
| `mono-font`                      | <Badge text="Deprecated" variant="danger" /> | `--font-mono`                                                    | CSS Variable                  |
| `font-size`                      | <Badge text="Deprecated" variant="danger" /> | `scale`                                                          | HTML Attribute                |
| `nav-bg-color`                   | <Badge text="Deprecated" variant="danger" /> | `::part(section-navbar)` or `--nav-background`                   | CSS Shadow Part / Variable    |
| `nav-text-color`                 | <Badge text="Deprecated" variant="danger" /> | `--nav-foreground` or `::part(section-navbar)`                   | CSS Variable / Shadow Part    |
| `nav-hover-bg-color`             | <Badge text="Deprecated" variant="danger" /> | `--nav-hover-bg` or `::part(nav-item):hover`                     | CSS Variable / Shadow Part    |
| `nav-hover-text-color`           | <Badge text="Deprecated" variant="danger" /> | `--nav-hover-fg` or `::part(nav-item):hover`                     | CSS Variable / Shadow Part    |
| `nav-accent-color`               | <Badge text="Deprecated" variant="danger" /> | `theme` or `--primary`                                           | HTML Attribute / CSS Variable |
| `nav-accent-text-color`          | <Badge text="Deprecated" variant="danger" /> | `--nav-accent-fg` (or `--primary-foreground` in `colored-block`) | CSS Variable                  |

---

## 3. Migration Details by Feature Area

### 3.1 Theme & Color Scheme Modernization

In v10, you configured dark mode and primary button colors using separate attributes:

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="v10 (Legacy)">
```html
<!-- v10: theme set the surface, primary-color set the accent -->
<rapi-doc
  spec-url="https://api.example.com/openapi.json"
  theme="dark"
  primary-color="#3b82f6"
  bg-color="#0f172a"
  text-color="#f8fafc"
></rapi-doc>
```
  </TabItem>

  <TabItem label="v11 (Modern)">
```html
<!-- v11: color-scheme sets surface, theme sets preset or hex -->
<rapi-doc
  spec-url="https://api.example.com/openapi.json"
  color-scheme="dark"
  theme="#3b82f6"
></rapi-doc>
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

> **Note: Automatic Contrast Calculation in v11**
> When you set `theme="#3b82f6"` (or any hex code), RapiDoc v11 automatically evaluates the luminance of your brand color. If the color is
>   light, it renders high-contrast black text on buttons and badges; if dark, it renders white text. You no longer need to manually tune text
>   contrast for primary buttons!

---

### 3.2 Replacing Color Attributes with CSS Custom Properties

Instead of configuring colors directly on HTML attributes, assign standard CSS custom properties on `<rapi-doc>` in your stylesheet or `<style>` block.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="v10 (Legacy Attributes)">
```html
<rapi-doc
  spec-url="https://api.example.com/openapi.json"
  bg-color="#0b1120"
  text-color="#e2e8f0"
  primary-color="#10b981"
></rapi-doc>
```
  </TabItem>

  <TabItem label="v11 (CSS Variables)">
```html
<style>
  rapi-doc {
    /* Surface and Text tokens */
    --background: #0b1120;
    --foreground: #e2e8f0;

    /* Primary Accent token */
    --primary: #10b981;
    --primary-foreground: #ffffff;

    /* Border token */
    --border: #1e293b;

}

</style>

<rapi-doc
spec-url="https://api.example.com/openapi.json"
color-scheme="dark"

> </rapi-doc>

````
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

### 3.3 Replacing Navigation Attributes with CSS Variables & Shadow Parts

In v10, sidebar styling required up to six distinct attributes. In v11, you can style the sidebar using clean CSS custom properties or standard `::part(section-navbar)` selectors.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="v10 (Legacy Attributes)">
```html
<rapi-doc
  spec-url="https://api.example.com/openapi.json"
  nav-bg-color="#0f172a"
  nav-text-color="#94a3b8"
  nav-hover-bg-color="#1e293b"
  nav-hover-text-color="#ffffff"
  nav-accent-color="#3b82f6"
  nav-accent-text-color="#ffffff"
></rapi-doc>
````

  </TabItem>

  <TabItem label="v11 (CSS Variables)">
```css
/* Style sidebar navigation with design tokens */
rapi-doc {
  --nav-background: #0f172a;
  --nav-foreground: #94a3b8;
  --nav-hover-bg: #1e293b;
  --nav-hover-fg: #ffffff;
  --nav-accent-fg: #3b82f6;
}
```
  </TabItem>

  <TabItem label="v11 (CSS Shadow Parts)">
```css
/* Advanced styling with gradients, frosted glass blur, and borders */
rapi-doc::part(section-navbar) {
  background: linear-gradient(180deg, #0f172a 0%, #020617 100%);
  border-right: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08);
  backdrop-filter: blur(12px);
}

/_ Sidebar header area (logo and filter input) _/
rapi-doc::part(section-navbar-header) {
border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.06);
padding: 16px;
}

````
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

<Aside type="caution" title="Token Renaming: --nav-hover-fg and --nav-accent-fg">
  The tokens `--nav-hover-fg` and `--nav-accent-fg` are the canonical CSS variables for navigation hover text and selected item text color in default `left-bar` mode. In `colored-block` mode, selected items use standard `--primary` and `--primary-foreground`. Pre-release references to `--nav-hover-text`, `--nav-accent`, and `--nav-accent-foreground` have been completely dropped without backward compatibility.
</Aside>

<Aside type="tip" title="Sidebar Item Density in v11">
  To adjust vertical spacing between navigation links in v11 without CSS hacks, use the new declarative attribute:
  `<rapi-doc nav-item-spacing="compact | default | relaxed"></rapi-doc>`.
</Aside>

---

### 3.4 Replacing Typography & Font Attributes

In v10, custom fonts were passed as comma-separated font strings in attributes. In v11, configure fonts using CSS variables, allowing seamless inheritance from your application design system or `@font-face` definitions.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="v10 (Legacy Attributes)">
```html
<rapi-doc
  spec-url="https://api.example.com/openapi.json"
  regular-font="'Inter', sans-serif"
  mono-font="'JetBrains Mono', monospace"
  font-size="large"
></rapi-doc>
````

  </TabItem>

  <TabItem label="v11 (CSS Variables & Scale)">
```html
<style>
  rapi-doc {
    /* Define typography tokens */
    --font-sans: 'Inter', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, sans-serif;
    --font-mono: 'JetBrains Mono', 'Fira Code', monospace;
  }
</style>

<rapi-doc
spec-url="https://api.example.com/openapi.json"
scale="lg"

> </rapi-doc>

````
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

#### Font Scaling Mapping Reference

| v10 `font-size` Value | v11 `scale` Equivalent | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `default` | `scale="default"` | 14px base typography with balanced proportions. |
| `large` | `scale="lg"` | 16px base typography, generous margins, and wider sidebar. |
| `largest` | `scale="lg"` | Scaled up for presentations or accessibility. |
| *(New)* | `scale="sm"` | Compact 13px base typography; ideal for embedded console widgets. |

---

### 3.5 Button & Component Styling via `::part()`

In v10, you could not customize individual buttons, search bars, or server cards without overriding entire themes. RapiDoc v11 provides W3C standard **CSS Shadow Parts** for internal elements.

```css
/* Style primary action buttons (TRY, execute, search) */
rapi-doc::part(btn-fill) {
  background: linear-gradient(135deg, #06b6d4 0%, #3b82f6 100%);
  border-radius: 8px;
  box-shadow: 0 4px 12px rgba(6, 182, 212, 0.25);
  font-weight: 600;
}

rapi-doc::part(btn-fill):hover {
  transform: translateY(-1px);
  box-shadow: 0 6px 16px rgba(6, 182, 212, 0.4);
}

/* Style the TRY button specifically */
rapi-doc::part(btn-try) {
  border-radius: 6px;
  font-weight: 700;
  letter-spacing: 0.05em;
}

/* Style server selection panel */
rapi-doc::part(section-servers) {
  background: rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.6);
  border: 1px solid rgba(56, 189, 248, 0.2);
  border-radius: 10px;
}
````

---

## 4. End-to-End Migration Examples

### Example 1: Corporate Dark Portal

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="v10 Syntax">
```html
<rapi-doc
  spec-url="https://petstore.swagger.io/v2/swagger.json"
  theme="dark"
  bg-color="#0d1117"
  text-color="#c9d1d9"
  header-color="#161b22"
  primary-color="#238636"
  regular-font="'Inter', sans-serif"
  mono-font="'Fira Code', monospace"
  nav-bg-color="#161b22"
  nav-text-color="#8b949e"
  nav-accent-color="#238636"
  font-size="default"
></rapi-doc>
```
  </TabItem>

  <TabItem label="v11 Syntax">
```html
<style>
  rapi-doc {
    --background: #0d1117;
    --foreground: #c9d1d9;
    --header-bg: #161b22;
    --font-sans: 'Inter', sans-serif;
    --font-mono: 'Fira Code', monospace;
    --nav-background: #161b22;
    --nav-foreground: #8b949e;
  }
</style>

<rapi-doc
spec-url="https://petstore.swagger.io/v2/swagger.json"
color-scheme="dark"
theme="#238636"
radius="md"
scale="default"

> </rapi-doc>

````
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

### Example 2: Light Mode with Corporate Indigo Accent

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="v10 Syntax">
```html
<rapi-doc
  spec-url="https://petstore.swagger.io/v2/swagger.json"
  theme="light"
  bg-color="#ffffff"
  text-color="#1e293b"
  primary-color="#4f46e5"
  nav-bg-color="#f8fafc"
  nav-text-color="#475569"
  nav-accent-color="#4f46e5"
></rapi-doc>
````

  </TabItem>

  <TabItem label="v11 Syntax">
```html
<rapi-doc
  spec-url="https://petstore.swagger.io/v2/swagger.json"
  color-scheme="light"
  theme="#4f46e5"
  radius="md"
></rapi-doc>
```
*(Notice how concise v11 is: `color-scheme="light"` sets the base surfaces, and `theme="#4f46e5"` automatically configures navigation accents and high-contrast button labels!)*
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## 5. Step-by-Step Migration Checklist

Follow these steps to migrate an existing application to RapiDoc v11:

<Steps>
1. **Update Package Dependency / CDN Link**
   Upgrade your `rapidoc` package or update the `<script>` tag:
   ```bash
   npm install rapidoc@latest
   ```

2. **Update the Base Surface Mode**
   Search your HTML templates for `theme="dark"` or `theme="light"`. Change them to:
   - `theme="dark"` $\rightarrow$ `color-scheme="dark"`
   - `theme="light"` $\rightarrow$ `color-scheme="light"`
   - _(Optional)_ Use `color-scheme="system"` to automatically match user OS preference.

3. **Migrate Primary Brand Colors**
   If you used `primary-color="#..."`, migrate to:
   - `<rapi-doc theme="#your-hex-color">` or
   - CSS: `rapi-doc { --primary: #your-hex-color; }`

4. **Convert Deprecated Color Attributes to CSS Variables**
   Remove `bg-color`, `text-color`, and `nav-*` attributes from `<rapi-doc>`. If you need custom values beyond the built-in presets, define them in CSS:

   ```css
   rapi-doc {
     --background: #...;
     --foreground: #...;
     --nav-background: #...;
   }
   ```

5. **Convert Font Attributes to CSS Typography Tokens**
   Remove `regular-font` and `mono-font` attributes. Declare them in CSS:

   ```css
   rapi-doc {
     --font-sans: 'YourFont', sans-serif;
     --font-mono: 'YourMono', monospace;
   }
   ```

6. **Convert `font-size` to `scale`**
   Change `font-size="large"` to `scale="lg"`.

7. **Take Advantage of `::part()` for Advanced Customization**
   Replace any awkward styling workarounds with standard CSS Shadow Parts (`rapi-doc::part(section-navbar)`, `rapi-doc::part(btn-fill)`, etc.).
   </Steps>

---

  </DocsCard>
  <DocsCard title="CSS Parts & Variables Reference" icon="file-css">
    Explore the full catalog of CSS Custom Properties and Shadow Parts available in RapiDoc. [Explore CSS Parts](/docs/rapidoc/theming/css-parts/)
  </DocsCard>
</CardGrid>

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/rapidoc/migration/v10-to-v11/
