# Migrating from RapiDoc v11 to v12

> Upgrade guide for RapiDoc v12. CSS variables now follow shadcn/ui naming (including --sidebar-* for navigation), every variable has a real default, and RapiDoc renders semantic h1–h6 headings.

RapiDoc **v12** cleans up the styling API. Theming uses the same CSS variable names as [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/theming), every variable RapiDoc reads now has a default defined on the element (no more "not defined" hooks in DevTools), and titles render as real `<h1>`–`<h6>` headings.

v12 has no compatibility aliases: rename the variables below in your CSS when you upgrade.

---

## 1. Renamed and removed CSS variables

| v11                                              | v12                                                                |
| :----------------------------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--font-regular`                                 | `--font-sans`                                                      |
| `--rapidoc-font`, `--portal-font`                | `--font-sans` (set on `rapi-doc`)                                  |
| `--rapidoc-font-mono`, `--portal-font-mono`      | `--font-mono` (set on `rapi-doc`)                                  |
| `--rapidoc-bg`, `--portal-bg`                    | `--background` (set on `rapi-doc`)                                 |
| `--rapidoc-fg`, `--portal-fg`                    | `--foreground` (set on `rapi-doc`)                                 |
| `--nav-hover-bg`                                 | `--sidebar-accent`                                                 |
| `--nav-hover-fg`                                 | `--sidebar-accent-foreground`                                      |
| `--nav-accent-fg`                                | `--sidebar-primary` (also colors the active item's left marker)    |
| `--nav-width`                                    | `--sidebar-width`                                                  |
| `--nav-item-padding`                             | `--sidebar-item-padding`                                           |
| `--nav-logo-max-height`                          | `--sidebar-logo-max-height`                                        |
| `--input-border`                                 | `--input` (now the shadcn/ui meaning: border color of form fields) |
| `--input` (as a background)                      | `--input-background`                                               |
| `--card-radius`, `--border-radius`               | `--radius` (cards and dialogs use `min(var(--radius), 0.5rem)`)    |
| `--code-fg`, `--markdown-fg`, `--inline-code-fg` | `--foreground`                                                     |
| `--inline-code-bg`                               | `--muted`                                                          |
| `--method-copy`, `--method-purge`                | `--method-default`                                                 |
| `--red` for errors and required markers          | `--destructive` (`--red` remains for `x-badges` colors)            |

Removed because setting them had no effect: `--code-property-color`, `--code-keyword-color`, `--code-operator-color`, `--ui-base-size`, `--scroll-bar-width`, `--layout`, `--primary-hover`, `--schema-description-threshold`, `--schema-field-name-threshold`.

Removed undocumented layout hooks: `--content-padding` and `--read-mode-bottom-padding` (style the `section-main-content` part instead).

New variables:

- `--sidebar`, `--sidebar-foreground`, `--sidebar-border`, `--sidebar-ring`: shadcn/ui sidebar tokens for the navigation bar.
- `--destructive`: errors, required-field markers, and DEPRECATED labels.
- `--scroll-margin-top` (default `120px`): space kept above a section when navigation scrolls to it.
- Heading scale: `--h1-font-size` … `--h6-font-size`, `--heading-font`, `--heading-weight`, `--heading-line-height`, `--heading-color`, `--heading-letter-spacing`, `--heading-margin-top`, `--heading-margin-bottom`, `--label-heading-font-size`, `--line-height`, `--paragraph-spacing`.
- `--font-size-xs` (default `11px`, `12px` with `scale="lg"`): the smallest text RapiDoc renders (badges, sidebar method tags, oneOf/anyOf chips, constraint labels, tiny buttons).
- `--font-size-description` (default `13px`, `12px` with `scale="sm"`, `15px` with `scale="lg"`): parameter, property, and response-header descriptions.

`--ring` now defaults to `var(--primary)` in every theme. In v11 it was missing for the default `amber` theme, so keyboard focus had no visible ring.

---

## 2. Using RapiDoc in a shadcn/ui site

Set variables on the `rapi-doc` element. A rule on the element overrides RapiDoc's built-in theme, and `inherit` takes the value from your page's `:root`, so a shadcn/ui theme carries over without copying values:

```css
rapi-doc {
  --background: inherit;
  --foreground: inherit;
  --card: inherit;
  --card-foreground: inherit;
  --primary: inherit;
  --primary-foreground: inherit;
  --muted: inherit;
  --muted-foreground: inherit;
  --border: inherit;
  --input: inherit;
  --radius: inherit;
  --sidebar: inherit;
  --sidebar-foreground: inherit;
  --sidebar-primary: inherit;
  --sidebar-accent: inherit;
  --sidebar-accent-foreground: inherit;
  --sidebar-border: inherit;
  --font-sans: inherit;
  --font-mono: inherit;
}
```

> **Caution: Don't reference a variable by its own name**
> `rapi-doc { --font-sans: var(--font-sans); }` refers to itself, which makes the variable invalid. Use `inherit`, or a different variable
>   such as `var(--my-font)`.

Variables set on an ancestor (`:root`, `body`) without this rule do not reach RapiDoc, because RapiDoc defines its own defaults on the element.

---

## 3. Semantic headings

RapiDoc titles are now real headings, so they share sizes and spacing with Markdown/MDX pages around them:

| Level | Content                                                           |
| :---- | :---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `h1`  | API title (the version is a badge, part `label-overview-version`) |
| `h2`  | API Server, Authentication, tag groups, tags                      |
| `h3`  | Operation summaries                                               |
| `h4`  | Request, Response, Code samples, Callbacks                        |
| `h5`  | Parameter, request body, and response header labels               |

All existing CSS parts are unchanged. New parts: `heading` and `heading-1` … `heading-6` on every generated heading, plus `section-auth-title`, `section-request-title`, and `section-response-title`.

Section titles are now written in normal case ("API Server", "Authentication"). The small labels (Request, Path parameters, …) still display in capitals through CSS.

---

## 4. Visual changes

- Inline code, markdown text, and code-block text follow the theme's `--foreground` and `--muted` instead of fixed colors.
- View-mode operation borders use the `--method-*` colors (same as the method badges).
- Headings are bolder (`600`) and larger, and paragraphs inside descriptions are `1em` apart.
- No text is smaller than `11px`. Sidebar method tags, oneOf/anyOf chips, and small badges were 9–10px; they now use `--font-size-xs`, which also follows the `scale` attribute.
- Parameter and property descriptions are `13px` (`--font-size-description`) instead of `12px`.
- Sidebar navigation text uses `--font-size-regular`, the body text size: `14px` instead of `13px` (`13px` with `scale="sm"`, `16px` with `scale="lg"`), with a `20px` line height instead of `16px`. Rows are a few pixels taller; use `nav-item-spacing="compact"` for very long API lists.
- The first label inside the Request panel (Path parameters, Request body, ...) sits right under the Request heading instead of `24px` below it.
- Markdown tables in descriptions are `display: block` and scroll horizontally inside their own box when wider than the space available, instead of widening the page.
- Buttons, inputs, and selects use two shared sizes that follow the `scale` attribute: default (~28px) for panel actions and form fields, small (~24px) for controls inside a panel. Inputs in parameter rows are taller (~35px) to line up with the two-line parameter label. Buttons are flat (no drop shadow).
- Copy buttons are small outline buttons. Their part changed from `btn btn-fill btn-copy` to `btn btn-outline btn-copy`; target `::part(btn-copy)` to style them.
- Read mode: tag groups (`x-tagGroups`) are a small muted uppercase label right above their first tag instead of a large `--primary` heading, and tag groups, tags, and operations are separated by one thin `--border` rule each (no `--primary` rules, no divider before a tag's first operation).
- Allowed values and examples next to a parameter are keyboard-focusable buttons drawn as compact accent links with a dotted underline (solid on hover and focus), and plain text when Try is off. Their parts are unchanged (`anchor-param-constraint`, `anchor-param-example`).
- Links use the theme's accent as text, `--primary-text`, instead of a fixed blue. `--primary-text` is `--primary` adjusted to be readable (4.5:1) in each color scheme (`--primary-text-dark`, `--primary-text-light`). Links in descriptions carry a quiet underline that turns solid on hover; other links are underlined on hover.
- Response status codes are a segmented control; the selected code is tinted with `--primary` instead of filled.
- An operation's authentication chips sit right under its method and path, before the description, after a lock icon. The "Authorization" label is kept for screen readers only.
- The chips no longer link to the Authentication section; they only open their details popover. The lock icon is the link now, and the `anchor-operation-security` part moved from the chip labels to it.

---

## 5. Parameter lists replace tables

Request parameters, request-body form fields, response headers, server variables, and the Authentication section were `<table role="presentation">` layouts. They are now lists on a CSS grid:

```html
<ul class="param-list" part="param-list" role="list">
  <li class="param" part="param">
    <div class="param-label" part="param-label">
      <div class="param-name" part="param-name">limit</div>
      <div class="param-type" part="param-type">int32</div>
    </div>
    <div class="param-input" part="param-input"><input part="textbox textbox-param" /></div>
    <div class="param-constraint" part="param-constraint">Min 1 | Max 100</div>
    <div class="param-details" part="param-details">Description and examples</div>
  </li>
</ul>
```

- **Layout.** The list is a three-column grid (`var(--param-label-width) minmax(10rem, 1fr) minmax(0, 1.5fr)`) and each `.param` is a subgrid row, so columns line up and every row's border reaches the edge. Without constraints the input spans both right-hand columns; without an input (`allow-try="false"`, response headers) the constraints do. Below about `36rem` of container width everything stacks in one column, with no horizontal scrolling.
- **One label width.** The label column was `200px` in read and focused mode and `160px` in view mode. It is now `--param-label-width` (`12rem`) everywhere.
- **Response headers** show name and type on the left, the schema example (as "Example:") in the constraints column, and the description below. The list is full width.
- **Constraints** are a definition list, `<dl class="param-constraint">`, with one `<dt>` label and `<dd>` value per constraint (Default, Pattern, Limits, Allowed). The labels share one column, so every value starts at the same place, whether there is one constraint or several. Range, multiple-of, and length limits, which had no label, are now under "Limits:" and wrap like allowed values. New part: `param-constraint-label`. When a parameter has constraints but no description, its short-format examples become the last row of this list ("Examples:"), lined up with the other values; otherwise they stay under the description.
- **Allowed values and short-format examples** are a `<div class="value-list">` with a label and a `<ul class="value-list-items">` of values. Wrapped lines line up under the first value, and the `┃` separators are drawn in CSS (`li::after`) so a line never starts with one. Long-format examples (with a summary or description) are a `<ul class="param-example-list" part="param-example-list">` with no marker (the v11 disclosure triangle looked clickable); each entry has a thin left rule, which turns `--primary` while the entry is hovered or its example link has focus.
- **Operation security chips** use the same value-list layout: `.operation-security` holds a `.security-label-group` ("Authorization" and the lock) and a `<ul class="value-list-items security-chips">` with one `<li>` per chip. Wrapped chips line up under the first chip, and `OR` is drawn in CSS at the end of each line, so the `.security-or` element is gone.
- **Authentication** is `<ul class="auth-list" id="auth-list" part="auth-list">` with one `<li id="security-scheme-{id}" class="auth-scheme {type}" part="auth-scheme">` per scheme; OAuth flows are in `<div class="auth-flows" part="auth-flows">` inside their scheme instead of a separate row.

| Removed                                                 | Use instead                                                       |
| :------------------------------------------------------ | :---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.m-table`, `.m-table.padded-12`, `tr` / `td` selectors | `.param-list`, `.param`, `.param-*`, `.auth-list`, `.auth-scheme` |
| `#auth-table`                                           | `#auth-list`, part `auth-list`                                    |
| Fixed `200px` / `160px` label column                    | `--param-label-width`                                             |

New CSS parts: `param-list`, `param`, `param-label`, `param-name`, `param-type`, `param-input`, `param-constraint`, `param-constraint-label`, `param-details`, `value-list`, `value-list-label`, `value-list-items`, `auth-list`, `auth-scheme`, and `auth-flows`. `anchor-param-constraint` is now exported from requests and responses as well.

New CSS variables: `--param-label-width`, `--param-gap`, `--param-row-gap`, `--param-padding`, `--value-list-gap`, `--value-list-row-gap`, `--value-list-label-gap`, and `--auth-scheme-padding`.

```css
rapi-doc {
  --param-label-width: 14rem;
}
rapi-doc::part(param) {
  padding-block: 0.75rem;
}
rapi-doc::part(param-name) {
  font-weight: 600;
}
```

---

## 6. No web fonts are loaded

v11 downloaded three weights of Open Sans from `fonts.gstatic.com` on every page unless you set `load-fonts="false"`, even though its own font list no longer used Open Sans. v12 makes no font requests: text uses `--font-sans` and `--font-mono`, which default to the operating system's UI and monospace fonts.

- The `load-fonts` attribute is removed. You can delete `load-fonts="false"` from your markup; leaving it in has no effect.
- To keep a brand font (Open Sans or any other), load it in your page and set `--font-sans` / `--font-mono` on `rapi-doc`. See [Typography & Brand Fonts](/docs/rapidoc/theming/overview/#4-fonts).

---

## 7. Five themes

The `theme` presets are reduced to five, each with a dark and a light palette: `ember` (default), `carbon`, `cobalt`, `jade` and `indigo`. See [Pre-built Themes](/docs/rapidoc/theming/prebuilt-themes/).

| v11 | v12 |
| :--- | :--- |
| `amber` (and no attribute) | `ember`: same `#f76b39` accent, neutral charcoal surfaces instead of blue-grey |
| `graphite` | `carbon`: same accents, near-black surfaces in dark mode |
| `blue` | `cobalt` (matte steel blue; pass `theme="#2563eb"` for the old electric blue) |
| `emerald` | `jade` |
| `violet` | `indigo` |
| `rose`, `slate`, `modern`, `default` | removed; pass a hex code (`theme="#e11d48"`) for an accent of your own |

The old names and a bare `#f76b39` are no longer special: an unknown name falls back to `ember`, and any hex code is a custom accent over the default surfaces.

Base surfaces also changed: dark `--background` is `#1f1f23` with `--foreground: #d4d4d8` (was a blue-grey `oklch` surface with `#cccccc`), and light `--foreground` is `#27272a` (was `#444444`). `color-scheme="system"` now derives its light-mode cards, borders and muted colors from the background and foreground exactly like `color-scheme="light"`.

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/rapidoc/migration/v11-to-v12/

---

# Migrating from RapiDoc v12 to v13

> Upgrade guide for RapiDoc v13. One filter-operations attribute replaces match-paths, match-type and remove-endpoints-with-badge-label-as on rapi-doc and rapi-doc-mini.

RapiDoc **v13** replaces the three attributes that chose which operations to show with one, `filter-operations`, on both `<rapi-doc>` and `<rapi-doc-mini>`. It names operations exactly (by operationId, or by method and path), takes path globs, tags and badges, and can exclude.

v13 has no compatibility aliases: the old attributes are ignored. Replace them when you upgrade.

---

## 1. Removed attributes

| v12 | v13 |
| :-- | :-- |
| `match-paths="get /pet/{petId}"` | `filter-operations="GET /pet/{petId}"` |
| `match-paths="/store"` (every path containing `/store`) | `filter-operations="/store/**"` (the path and everything under it) |
| `match-paths="^post /users$\|^get /users/\{id\}$"` with `match-type="regex"` | `filter-operations="POST /users GET /users/{id}"` |
| `match-type` | removed: no substring or regular expression matching |
| `remove-endpoints-with-badge-label-as="Beta, Internal"` | `filter-operations="!badge:Beta !badge:Internal"` |

> **Caution:**
> `match-paths` matched a **substring** of `"<method> <path>"`: `match-paths="get /pet"` also showed `GET /pet/findByStatus` and `GET /petition`. `filter-operations` matches **exactly**. To keep a prefix match, use a glob: `/pet/**`.

## 2. What a term can be

A space- or comma-separated list. An operation is shown when it matches any include term (every operation is, without one) and no `!` term.

| Term | Matches |
| :-- | :-- |
| `getPetById` | the operation with that operationId |
| `GET /pet/{petId}` | that method and path |
| `/pet/{petId}` | every method on that path |
| `/pet/*`, `/pet/**` | `*` is one path segment, `**` any number (the path itself too) |
| `tag:store` | operations tagged `store` (`tag:"Pet Store"` for a name with spaces) |
| `badge:Beta` | operations with that `x-badges` label |
| `deprecated` | deprecated operations |
| `!<term>` | leaves out what the term matches |

Paths, methods, tags and badges compare without case; operationIds exactly. An `operationId` is matched only when the term is none of the other kinds: an id that starts with `tag:` or `badge:`, or is the word `deprecated`, is read as that kind instead. Select such an operation by its method and path (`GET /path`). Operations are listed in the order of the first term they match, so `filter-operations="placeOrder getPetById"` shows `placeOrder` first. `sort-endpoints-by`, when set, decides the order instead.

## 3. Build-time rendering and the portal

- **`@rapidoc/prerender`**: `renderRapiDoc({ filterOperations })` (or `"filter-operations"`) replaces `matchPaths`, `matchType` and `removeEndpointsWithBadgeLabelAs`.
- **`@rapidoc/portal`**: the `{% api-operation %}` tag sets `filter-operations="<METHOD> <path>"` on its `<rapi-doc-mini>`; nothing changes in your Markdoc.

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/rapidoc/migration/v12-to-v13/

---

# Migrating from RapiDoc v13 to v14

> Upgrade guide for RapiDoc v14. Nothing changes in how you use rapi-doc; v14 marks the spec loading and schema code now shared with RapiPdf.

RapiDoc **v14** needs no changes on your side. No attribute, method, event, slot, part or CSS variable of `<rapi-doc>`, `<rapi-doc-mini>` or `<rapi-flow>` was added, renamed or removed. Update the version and you are done.

---

## 1. Why a new major

The code that loads a spec and reads its schemas is now shared between `<rapi-doc>` and **RapiPdf**. `rapipdf` 3 is built on the same loader and the same schema tree, so a PDF and the page read a spec the same way, and a fix to either reaches both.

- The [`rapidoc pdf`](/docs/cli/pdf/) command writes the API reference of a spec as a PDF.
- The [`<rapi-pdf>`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/rapipdf) element does the same in the browser.

## 2. What to update

| You use | Do this |
| :-- | :-- |
| `<rapi-doc>` from a CDN or npm | Move to `rapidoc@14`. Nothing else. |
| `@rapidoc/embed`, `@rapidoc/starlight`, `@rapidoc/vitepress` or `@rapidoc/docusaurus` | Update the integration too: its new release asks for `rapidoc ^14.0.0`. |
| `@rapidoc/cli` and `@rapidoc/portal` | Update them together, as with every release. |
| `rapipdf` 2 | See the [`rapipdf` changelog](https://www.npmjs.com/package/rapipdf) for what changed in 3. |

## 3. One fix in this release

A schema that contains itself is marked as recursive at the property that refers back to it. In some specs the marker landed one level down, and the property was drawn as an object with a single `$ref` member.

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/rapidoc/migration/v13-to-v14/

---

# In-Browser Mock

> Answer API requests inside the page from your OpenAPI spec with the mock-server attribute, with no server to run.

Add `mock-server="true"` to `<rapi-doc>` or `<rapi-doc-mini>` and requests to your API are answered in the page, from the spec's examples and schemas. Nothing is deployed and nothing leaves the browser. Readers can press **Try** on a published page and get a sensible answer, and you can build and demo a frontend before the backend exists.

> **Tip: See it running**
> The [in-browser mock example](/examples/mock-server) has a live testbed: pick a status code and a delay, and call the API. For a real HTTP server that any client can call, with request validation and token checks, see [RapiMock](https://mock.rapidocui.com/); [In the page or as a server](#in-the-page-or-as-a-server) compares the two.

## Turn it on

```html
<rapi-doc
  spec-url="https://rapidocui.com/specs/petstore.yaml"
  mock-server="true"
></rapi-doc>
```

`<rapi-doc>` then shows a pulsing dot and a **MOCKING** label in its API Server section.

The mock patches the page's `fetch` and `XMLHttpRequest`. A request whose method and path match an operation in the spec is answered by the mock; every other request (analytics, images, other APIs) goes to the network as usual. That means it answers not only **Try**, but any script on the same page:

```javascript
const doc = document.querySelector('rapi-doc');
doc.addEventListener('spec-loaded', () => {
  // The mock starts right after spec-loaded, so call it on the next tick
  setTimeout(async () => {
    const res = await fetch('https://petstore3.swagger.io/api/v3/pet/findByStatus?status=available');
    console.log(await res.json()); // from the spec, not the real API
  });
});
```

Only operations that `<rapi-doc>` shows are mocked: endpoints left out by a `<rapi-doc-mini>` filter, for example, go to the network.

## Attributes

| Attribute | Default | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `mock-server` | `false` | `true` turns the mock on. Setting it back to `false` turns it off. |
| `mock-server-status-code` | `200` | The status code to answer with, a comma-separated list used in turn (`"503, 503, 200"`), the same with a strategy in front (`"random:200, 500"`), or a JSON map by operation (see below). Set it to `""` to use the first `2xx` response in the spec (else `default`, else the first response listed). |
| `mock-server-status-strategy` | `cycle` | **Deprecated**: write the strategy in front of the codes instead. How codes without a prefix are picked: `cycle`, `random` or `first`. |
| `mock-server-delay` | `0` | Milliseconds to wait before answering, to show loading states. For a streamed response, the gap between its items (300 ms when `0`). |
| `mock-server-log` | `false` | `true` logs each answered request to the browser console. |

## Simulating errors

Give `mock-server-status-code` several codes, with the strategy in front of them when it isn't `cycle`:

```html
<rapi-doc
  spec-url="/specs/api.yaml"
  mock-server="true"
  mock-server-status-code="503, 503, 200"
></rapi-doc>
```

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="cycle (default)">
    `503, 503, 200` or `cycle:503, 503, 200`. Each operation steps through the list in turn: the first call gets `503`, the second `503`, the third `200`, and then it starts again. Use it to test retries and error messages.
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="random">
    `random:200, 429, 503`. Every call gets a code picked at random from the list. Use it to check that the UI copes with failures it doesn't expect.
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="one code">
    `401`. Every call gets it, which shows how a page behaves when the user is signed out. (`first:` exists for older pages; one code does the same.)
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

Each operation's place in its list starts again whenever the codes change. Earlier versions gave a list without a prefix only its first code unless `mock-server-status-strategy="cycle"` was set; that attribute still sets the strategy for codes without a prefix, but a prefix is clearer and can differ per operation.

### Per-operation status codes

To make one operation fail while the others succeed, pass a JSON map. Keys are the method and path template from the spec; `"*"` applies to every other operation. Each entry has its own list and its own strategy, and a list cycles for that operation only:

```html
<rapi-doc
  spec-url="/specs/petstore.yaml"
  mock-server="true"
  mock-server-status-code='{ "POST /store/order": "503, 200", "GET /store/inventory": "random:200, 500", "*": "200" }'
></rapi-doc>
```

The same value can be set as an object on the `mockServerStatusCode` property. [`<rapi-flow>`](https://flow.rapidocui.com/docs/running/#running-against-a-mock) sets it from its Mock Response Status table for the length of a run.

## What the mock answers

For the chosen status code, the mock builds the response from the spec's response object:

1. **Body**: the media type's `example`; else the first entry of its `examples`; else the schema's `example`; else a value generated from the schema. Generated values use `enum`, `default`, `minimum`/`maximum`, `pattern` and `format` where they can (`user@example.com` for `email`, a UUID for `uuid`), and `writeOnly` properties are left out. JSON is preferred over XML, and XML over text.
2. **No body in the spec**: JSON responses get `{ "status": <code>, "message": "<status text>" }`, other types get the status text, and `204` gets an empty body.
3. **Headers**: response headers from the spec, filled from their `example` or schema `default`, plus `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` and `X-Mock-Server: RapiDoc`.
4. **Streams** (an OpenAPI 3.2 `itemSchema` on `text/event-stream`, JSON Lines or `application/json-seq`): the response starts at once and sends one item at a time, `mock-server-delay` apart (300 ms when `0`), so **Try** shows it arriving and its **STOP** button can end it. The items are those of the first example (a `dataValue` list, or the stream's text split into events or lines); without one, an item generated from the `itemSchema` is sent 5 times, its `id` numbered 1 to 5. Through `XMLHttpRequest` the whole stream comes at once.

## Mocking your app during development

Because the mock patches the page's `fetch`, your own frontend code in the same page is answered too. Add a hidden `<rapi-doc>` while you develop:

```html title="index.html"
<script type="module" src="https://unpkg.com/rapidoc/dist/rapidoc-min.js"></script>
<rapi-doc spec-url="/openapi.yaml" mock-server="true" mock-server-delay="200" style="display: none"></rapi-doc>
<div id="root"></div>
```

```javascript
// Anywhere in your app: answered from openapi.yaml, no backend needed
const user = await fetch('/api/v1/users/me').then((res) => res.json());
```

Matched requests never reach the network, so cross-origin (CORS) rules don't get in the way. For calls from other programs, or from a different page, use the [mock server](https://mock.rapidocui.com/) instead.

## Console log

With `mock-server-log="true"`, every answered request prints one line:

```text
[RapiDoc Mock] GET /users/42 ➔ 200 OK
```

Requests made with `XMLHttpRequest` are tagged `[RapiDoc Mock (XHR)]`.

## Several mocks on one page

Each element with `mock-server="true"` mocks its own spec with its own status codes and delay, so one page can mock two APIs:

```html
<rapi-doc-mini spec-url="/specs/orders.yaml" mock-server="true" filter-operations="POST /orders"></rapi-doc-mini>
<rapi-doc-mini spec-url="/specs/payments.yaml" mock-server="true" mock-server-status-code="402"></rapi-doc-mini>
```

A request goes to the most specific match: a route under the request's server origin and base path wins over the same path under another API's base path, which wins over a bare path.

When an element turns its mock off or is removed from the page, its routes stop being answered. The page's real `fetch` and `XMLHttpRequest` come back when no element is mocking any more.

## In the page or as a server

The in-browser mock answers code running in the same page: **Try**, `<rapi-flow>` and the page's own scripts. [RapiMock](https://mock.rapidocui.com/), RapiDoc's mock server (`rapidoc mock`), answers any client over HTTP.

| | In-browser mock | RapiMock |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **How you turn it on** | `mock-server="true"` on `<rapi-doc>` or `<rapi-doc-mini>` | `npx rapidoc mock openapi.yaml` |
| **Runs** | Inside the page, by intercepting `fetch` | As a Node HTTP server (default port `4010`) |
| **Who can call it** | Code running in the same page | Any client: curl, your frontend, tests, MCP servers |
| **Choosing a status code** | `mock-server-status-code`, per operation if needed | `Prefer: code=…` request header |
| **Request validation, token and scope checks** | No | Yes |
| **Remembers what you create** | No: every call is answered on its own | Yes, with `--stateful` |

**Pick the in-browser mock** for docs and demos: readers can press **Try** on a published page and get a sensible answer, with nothing to deploy. **Pick RapiMock** for development and testing: when other programs need to call the API, when requests and tokens should be checked the way production checks them, or when a test has to create something and read it back. Its [quickstart](https://mock.rapidocui.com/docs/getting-started/quickstart/) starts one in a minute, and [Testing with RapiDoc](https://mock.rapidocui.com/docs/testing/with-rapidoc/) points `<rapi-doc>` at it.

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/rapidoc/mocking/in-browser/

---

# Large Specs

> Keep RapiDoc fast with specs of several megabytes and thousands of operations.

RapiDoc renders specs with over a thousand operations, but large specs need the right settings. In order of impact:

## 1. Use `view` or `focused` mode

`read` mode renders every operation at once. On an 8 MB spec with 1,128 operations it takes about 6 seconds, against about 1 second in `view` or `focused` mode (see [Render Modes](/docs/rapidoc/performance/render-modes/#measured-load-times)).

```html
<rapi-doc spec-url="/openapi.json" render-style="focused"></rapi-doc>
```

## 2. Convert Swagger 2.0 ahead of time

A Swagger 2.0 spec is upgraded to OpenAPI 3.x in the reader's browser on every page load. For a large spec, convert it once in your build instead:

<Steps>

1. Convert the spec:

   ```bash
   npx swagger2openapi swagger.json --outfile openapi.json
   ```

2. Point RapiDoc at the converted file:

   ```html
   <rapi-doc spec-url="/openapi.json"></rapi-doc>
   ```

</Steps>

## 3. Collapse schemas

By default, schemas start fully expanded. Large, deeply nested schemas render faster when they start collapsed:

```html
<rapi-doc
  spec-url="/openapi.json"
  render-style="focused"
  schema-expand-level="1"
  default-schema-tab="schema"
></rapi-doc>
```

- `schema-expand-level="1"`: only the first level of each schema is open; readers expand the rest.
- `default-schema-tab="schema"`: request and response bodies open on the schema tab instead of the example tab, so example blocks aren't drawn until a reader opens them.

## 4. Mind the structure, not just the size

File size matters less than structure. Long Markdown descriptions cost little; what slows rendering is the number of operations and how large and deeply nested their schemas are once `$ref`s are resolved. A schema referenced by hundreds of operations is rendered once for each of them.

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/rapidoc/performance/large-specs/

---

# Render Modes

> Compare RapiDoc's read, view and focused render styles, with measured load times on large specs.

The `render-style` attribute decides how `<rapi-doc>` lays out operations. It is also the setting that matters most for large specs.

```html
<rapi-doc spec-url="/openapi.yaml" render-style="focused"></rapi-doc>
```

## The three modes

### `read` (default)

One long page: the overview, then every tag and operation, fully rendered, with a sidebar that follows as you scroll. Good for small and medium APIs that readers go through from top to bottom. Because everything is rendered, load time grows with the size of the spec.

### `view`

Tags with collapsible operations. Several operations can be open at once, and collapsed ones aren't rendered until they are opened, so the page stays light. Search is in the header. Good for most APIs.

### `focused`

A sidebar listing every operation, and one operation at a time in the main area. Only the selected operation is rendered, so it stays fast on very large specs and on slow devices.

## Measured load times

Time to load, parse and render, measured in headless Chrome with RapiDoc 11.0.0:

| Spec | Size | Operations | `focused` | `view` | `read` |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Bookstore (OpenAPI 3.2) | 13.8 KB | 12 | ~56 ms | ~37 ms | ~31 ms |
| Stripe (OpenAPI 3.0, deep schemas) | 7.00 MB | 644 | ~666 ms | ~650 ms | ~9.22 s |
| GitHub (OpenAPI 3.1) | 8.19 MB | 1,128 | ~997 ms | ~990 ms | ~5.95 s |

On small specs the mode makes no difference. On large ones, `read` is many times slower than the other two. The [performance tests](/tests/performance) have the details and the scripts that produce them.

> **Tip: Which one to choose**
> If you don't know how large the specs you'll show will get, use `view` or `focused`. Keep `read` for specs of up to a few hundred operations.

## Switching modes at runtime

`render-style` can be changed at any time, for example from a toggle in your page:

```javascript
document.querySelector('rapi-doc').setAttribute('render-style', 'read');
```

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/rapidoc/performance/render-modes/

---

# React to Events

> Change Try requests before they are sent, read responses, and react to spec loading, server changes and navigation with <rapi-doc> events.

`<rapi-doc>` dispatches DOM events you can listen to with `addEventListener`. The full list, with every field, is in the [API reference](/docs/rapidoc/reference/events/).

## Change a request before it is sent: `before-try`

`before-try` fires when a reader presses **Try**, before the request goes out. `e.detail.request` is a plain object you can change:

| Field | Type |
| :--- | :--- |
| `url` | `string`: can be replaced |
| `method` | `string` |
| `headers` | `Headers`: add, change or delete headers |
| `body` | the request body |
| `credentials` | the `fetch` credentials mode |

`e.detail.controller` is the request's `AbortController`; call `abort()` to cancel it.

```javascript
const doc = document.querySelector('rapi-doc');

doc.addEventListener('before-try', (e) => {
  const { request } = e.detail;
  request.headers.set('X-Correlation-ID', crypto.randomUUID());

  if (request.url.includes('/billing/')) {
    request.headers.set('X-Audit', 'strict');
  }
});
```

> **Caution: Listeners must be synchronous**
> RapiDoc reads the request as soon as the event returns, so it doesn't wait for promises. Work out any value you need (a signature, a fresh token) before the reader presses **Try**, and set it here synchronously.

## Read the response: `after-try`

`after-try` fires when the response arrives:

| Field | Type |
| :--- | :--- |
| `request` | the `Request` that was sent |
| `response` | a clone of the `Response` |
| `responseHeaders` | the response headers |
| `responseBody` | the parsed body |
| `responseStatus` | `boolean`: `true` for a 2xx status |

If the request fails at the network level, `detail` is `{ err, request }` instead.

```javascript
doc.addEventListener('after-try', (e) => {
  if (e.detail.err) return;
  analytics.track('Try', {
    url: e.detail.request.url,
    status: e.detail.response.status,
  });
});
```

To measure how long a request took, note `performance.now()` in `before-try` and compare in `after-try`.

## React to the spec: `before-render` and `spec-loaded`

- `before-render` fires after the spec is parsed and before it is rendered. `e.detail.spec` is the parsed spec; changes you make to it show up in the page.
- `spec-loaded` fires when rendering is done. `e.detail` is the parsed spec itself (`info`, `tags`, `servers`, `securitySchemes`, …).

```javascript
doc.addEventListener('spec-loaded', (e) => {
  console.log(`${e.detail.info.title}: ${e.detail.servers.length} server(s)`);
});
```

## Server changes: `api-server-change`

Fires when the reader picks another server in the API Servers section. `e.detail.selectedServer` is the server object: `url`, `description`, `variables` and `computedUrl` (the URL with its variables filled in).

```javascript
doc.addEventListener('api-server-change', (e) => {
  if (e.detail.selectedServer.url.includes('production')) {
    showWarning('Try now calls the production API.');
  }
});
```

## Every event

The [reference](/docs/rapidoc/reference/events/) lists every event and its `detail`. Two have guides of their own: `nav-active-change`, in [Links & Navigation](/docs/rapidoc/customizing/linking/#in-a-single-page-app), and the OAuth events `before-authorize` and `before-token-request`, in [OAuth 2.0](/docs/rapidoc/authentication/oauth/#from-javascript).

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/rapidoc/programmatic-api/event-hooks/

---

# Control It from JavaScript

> Load specs, set credentials, select servers and navigate <rapi-doc> from JavaScript.

`<rapi-doc>` is a DOM element, so you control it from JavaScript like any other: set attributes, call its methods and listen to its [events](/docs/rapidoc/programmatic-api/event-hooks/). The full list of methods is in the [API reference](/docs/rapidoc/reference/methods/).

## Wait until it is ready

Methods that work on the spec need the spec to be loaded. Wait for `spec-loaded`:

```javascript
const doc = document.querySelector('rapi-doc');
doc.addEventListener('spec-loaded', (e) => {
  console.log('Loaded', e.detail.info.title);
});
```

If your script may run before the RapiDoc bundle, wait for the element to be defined first: `await customElements.whenDefined('rapi-doc')`.

## Load a spec: `loadSpec(specOrUrl)`

Takes a spec object or a URL. Useful when you fetch the spec yourself, or switch between specs:

```javascript
async function showTenant(tenantId) {
  const res = await fetch(`/api/specs/${tenantId}.json`);
  doc.loadSpec(await res.json());
}
```

## Set credentials: `setApiKey(schemeId, value, options?)`

Fills in the credential of a security scheme, so readers don't have to. `schemeId` is the scheme's name under `components.securitySchemes`. For an HTTP bearer scheme, RapiDoc adds the `Bearer ` prefix.

```javascript
// After your app signs the user in
doc.setApiKey('BearerAuth', sessionToken);
```

Pass `{ note }` to say where the credential came from. The Authentication section then shows the note instead of that scheme's form, with a **Use a different token** link that opens the form. Changing or removing the key removes the note.

```javascript
doc.setApiKey('BearerAuth', sessionToken, { note: 'Using your sign-in (ann@example.com).' });
```

Related methods: `setHttpUserNameAndPassword(schemeId, username, password)` for HTTP Basic, and `removeAllSecurityKeys()`.

## Select a server: `setApiServer(url)`

Selects one of the spec's `servers` by URL, as if the reader had picked it. It returns `false` and changes nothing when the URL is not in the spec's `servers`. To send requests to a URL that isn't listed, set the `server-url` attribute instead.

```javascript
document.getElementById('env-select').addEventListener('change', (e) => {
  doc.setApiServer(e.target.value);
});
```

## Navigate: `scrollToPath(id)`

Scrolls to a section, tag or operation and opens it. Takes an [element ID](/docs/rapidoc/customizing/linking/#element-ids) or an operation's method and path:

```javascript
doc.scrollToPath('get-pet-by-id');     // by operation ID
doc.scrollToPath('get-/pet/{petId}');  // by method and path
doc.scrollToPath('tag--store');        // a tag
```

`scrollTo(id)` does the same.

## Example: your own toolbar

With `show-header="false"`, you can build the controls into your own page:

```html
<div class="toolbar">
  <select id="env-picker">
    <option value="https://petstore.swagger.io/v2">Production</option>
    <option value="http://petstore.swagger.io/v2">Production (HTTP)</option>
  </select>
  <button id="jump-login">Jump to login</button>
</div>

<rapi-doc
  id="the-doc"
  spec-url="https://petstore.swagger.io/v2/swagger.json"
  render-style="focused"
  show-header="false"
  style="height: calc(100vh - 50px)"
></rapi-doc>

<script>
  const doc = document.getElementById('the-doc');
  document.getElementById('env-picker').addEventListener('change', (e) => doc.setApiServer(e.target.value));
  document.getElementById('jump-login').addEventListener('click', () => doc.scrollToPath('get-/user/login'));
</script>
```

The options must be URLs from the spec's `servers` list.

> **Tip:**
> Methods for MCP export (`generateMcpServer`, `downloadMcpServer`, `getMcpBudget`) are described on [MCP Server](/docs/rapidoc/mcp-export/#from-javascript), and `bindNavBar` in [Pre-rendering](/docs/prerender/#a-static-sidebar).

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/rapidoc/programmatic-api/lifecycle-and-methods/

# Events

> Every event <rapi-doc> dispatches, with its detail, read from the element's source.

CustomEvents dispatched by `<rapi-doc>`. Listen with `addEventListener`; the payload is in `event.detail`. How to use them is in [React to Events](/docs/rapidoc/programmatic-api/event-hooks/).

```js
const doc = document.querySelector('rapi-doc');

// Before a Try request is sent: add a header
doc.addEventListener('before-try', (e) => {
  e.detail.request.headers.append('X-Tenant-ID', 'acme');
});

// The reader picked another server
doc.addEventListener('api-server-change', (e) => {
  console.log('Server:', e.detail.selectedServer);
});
```

# Styling with CSS

> Style any element inside RapiDoc's Shadow DOM with CSS custom properties and ::part() selectors, with recipes.

The [theming attributes](/docs/rapidoc/theming/overview/) cover colors, radius and scale. For anything else, RapiDoc offers two hooks into its Shadow DOM, where ordinary CSS selectors can't reach:

- **CSS custom properties**, set on `rapi-doc`, change colors, fonts and sizes everywhere they are used.
- **CSS parts**, selected with `rapi-doc::part(name)`, style one kind of element directly.

---

## 1. Using `::part()`

In your page's CSS, write `rapi-doc::part(name)`:

```css
/* Target the navigation sidebar panel inside RapiDoc */
rapi-doc::part(section-navbar) {
  background: linear-gradient(180deg, #090d16 0%, #030712 100%);
  border-right: 1px solid rgba(56, 189, 248, 0.15);
  box-shadow: 4px 0 24px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4);
}

/* Target the header wrapper inside the navigation bar */
rapi-doc::part(section-navbar-header) {
  border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08);
  padding: 16px;
}
```

> **Tip: Pseudo-classes**
> Parts work with pseudo-classes such as `:hover`, `:focus` and `:active`: `rapi-doc::part(btn-fill):hover`.

---

## 2. All CSS parts

Every part, with what it selects, is in the [reference](/docs/rapidoc/reference/css/#css-parts).

---

## 3. CSS custom properties

Set variables on `rapi-doc` in your stylesheet or inline style:

```css
rapi-doc {
  /* Override surface tokens */
  --background: #0b1121;
  --foreground: #f8fafc;
  --card: #0f172a;
  --border: #1e293b;

  /* Override typography tokens */
  --font-sans: 'Inter', sans-serif;
  --font-mono: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace;

  /* Override radius token */
  --radius: 8px;
}
```

Every variable, with its default, is in the [reference](/docs/rapidoc/reference/css/#css-custom-properties).

---

### Headings

RapiDoc's titles are real headings, in one outline: the API title is `h1`; servers, authentication, tag groups and tags are `h2`; operation summaries `h3`; Request, Response, Code samples and Callbacks `h4`; parameter, request-body and response-header labels `h5`; a callback's request and response `h6`. Headings in your Markdown descriptions use the same scale, so both line up.

Change the scale with custom properties, or style one level with the `heading-1` … `heading-6` parts (every heading also has the `heading` part):

```css
rapi-doc {
  --heading-weight: 600;
  --heading-line-height: 1.2;
  --line-height: 1.75;
  --h1-font-size: 2.25rem;
  --h2-font-size: 1.75rem;
  --h3-font-size: 1.375rem;
}

rapi-doc::part(heading-2) {
  border-bottom: 1px solid #334155;
  padding-bottom: 0.25em;
}
```

## 4. Recipes

### Frosted-glass sidebar

```css
/* Frosted glass backdrop blur on sidebar */
rapi-doc::part(section-navbar) {
  background: rgba(10, 15, 26, 0.85);
  backdrop-filter: blur(16px);
  -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(16px);
  border-right: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08);
}

/* Sidebar header area (wrapping logo & search) */
rapi-doc::part(section-navbar-header) {
  padding: 16px;
  border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.06);
}

/* Real-time search filter input inside sidebar */
rapi-doc::part(textbox-nav-filter) {
  background: rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.6);
  border: 1px solid rgba(56, 189, 248, 0.2);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  color: #f8fafc;
  padding: 8px 12px;
}

rapi-doc::part(textbox-nav-filter):focus {
  border-color: #06b6d4;
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(6, 182, 212, 0.2);
}
```

### Gradient buttons

```css
/* Base button enhancements */
rapi-doc::part(btn) {
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  font-weight: 600;
  transition: all 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1);
}

/* Primary filled buttons, such as TRY */
rapi-doc::part(btn-fill) {
  background: linear-gradient(135deg, #06b6d4 0%, #3b82f6 100%);
  color: #ffffff;
  border: none;
  padding: 8px 16px;
  box-shadow: 0 4px 12px rgba(6, 182, 212, 0.25);
}

rapi-doc::part(btn-fill):hover {
  transform: translateY(-1px);
  box-shadow: 0 6px 16px rgba(6, 182, 212, 0.4);
}
```

### Server panel

```css
/* Server selector container */
rapi-doc::part(section-servers) {
  background: rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.7);
  border: 1px solid rgba(56, 189, 248, 0.2);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  padding: 16px 20px;
}

/* Selected base URL indicator */
rapi-doc::part(label-selected-server) {
  color: #38bdf8;
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  font-weight: 600;
}
```

> **Tip: Which to use**
> Set the basics with attributes (`theme`, `color-scheme`, `radius`, `scale`) and variables, and keep `::part()` for what they can't do, such as gradients, backdrop filters and borders on specific containers.

---

<a id="schema-sizing-and-truncation"></a>

## 5. Schema descriptions

In both **Tree mode** and **Table mode**, each schema row shows its description on a single line. Click a description (or its `➔` arrow) to expand that row, and click again to collapse it. The **Multiline description** toolbar button expands every row at once.

### Layout Differences

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="Tree Mode Structure">
    In **Tree mode**, property names, data types, constraints, and descriptions are displayed in a continuous, hierarchically indented horizontal line:

    <div style="margin: 16px 0; border-radius: 8px; overflow: hidden; border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.1);">
      <img src="/assets/images/schema-tree-mode.png" alt="RapiDoc Schema Tree Mode Structure" style="width: 100%; display: block;" />
    </div>

    - **Field Column**: Has a dynamic minimum column width (`min-width: calc(400px - indent)`).
    - **Long Property Names**: Truncated with an ellipsis, with the full name in a hover tooltip (`title="..."`). Expanding the row also shows the full name.

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Table Mode Structure">
    In **Table mode**, the schema is formatted into a strict 3-column CSS subgrid:

    <div style="margin: 16px 0; border-radius: 8px; overflow: hidden; border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.1);">
      <img src="/assets/images/schema-table-mode.png" alt="RapiDoc Schema Table Mode Structure" style="width: 100%; display: block;" />
    </div>

    - **Field Column (`.key`)**: Dedicated column with a width controlled by `--table-schema-key-width` (default: `240px`). Long property names truncate with an ellipsis and show full text via hover tooltips (`title="..."`).
    - **Type Column (`.key-type`)**: Fixed minimum column (~150px) displaying data types and nullability badges.
    - **Description Column (`.key-descr`)**: Flexible `1fr` column spanning the remaining container width.

  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

### What a collapsed row shows

| Description content                                                   | Collapsed row                                                                                              | `➔` arrow                   |
| :-------------------------------------------------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :-------------------------- |
| One paragraph that fits                                               | The whole paragraph                                                                                        | No                          |
| One paragraph that is too long for the column                         | The start of the paragraph, cut off with an ellipsis                                                       | Chrome and Edge (see below) |
| Several paragraphs, a list with several items, or a `<br>` line break | The first paragraph or list item                                                                           | Yes                         |
| A table, code block, HTML block or blockquote first                   | A one-line summary: `Table · 3 rows`, `Code block · json`, the text of the HTML, or the quote's first line | Yes                         |
| A heading first                                                       | The heading text, at description size                                                                      | Yes, when more follows      |
| A schema `title` before a list, heading, table or code block          | `Title:` and the first line of that block                                                                  | Yes                         |
| A description plus constraints, default, allowed values or pattern    | The description; the constraint chips are hidden                                                           | Yes                         |
| Constraints only, no description                                      | The constraint chips                                                                                       | No                          |
| Nothing                                                               | An empty cell                                                                                              | No                          |

Whether a line is too long is decided by the browser at the actual column width and font, not by counting characters, so it adapts to split panes, sidebars and resizing without any JavaScript.

### Long lines

A cut-off line always ends with a plain ellipsis in the text color. The `➔` arrow is the only control.

- **Chrome and Edge (133+)**: a row whose line is cut off also shows the `➔` arrow and a pointer cursor. This uses a CSS [scroll-state container query](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/css-scroll-state-queries).
- **Other browsers**: the ellipsis is the only cue. Clicking the text still expands the row.

An expanded row keeps its arrow, pointing up, so it can be collapsed again. A row with nothing more to show (a line that fits, and no arrow) doesn't react to clicks.

```css
rapi-doc {
  /* Allocate more width for property names in Table mode */
  --table-schema-key-width: 300px;
}
```

---

## 6. Parameter Lists

Request parameters, request-body form fields, response headers, and server variables share one layout: a `<ul part="param-list">` grid with one `<li part="param">` per parameter. Each parameter is a subgrid row with up to four pieces:

| Part               | Column | Content                                                                           |
| :----------------- | :----- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `param-label`      | 1      | `param-name` (required marker, deprecated icon) and `param-type`                  |
| `param-input`      | 2      | Try-it input; spans columns 2–3 when there are no constraints                     |
| `param-constraint` | 3      | Default, pattern, range, allowed values; spans columns 2–3 when there is no input |
| `param-details`    | 2–3    | Description and examples, on the next row                                         |

Allowed values and short-format examples are a `value-list`: a `value-list-label` followed by `value-list-items`. Wrapped values line up under the first value, and the `┃` separators are drawn in CSS so they stay at the end of a line. Space them with `--value-list-gap`, `--value-list-row-gap`, and `--value-list-label-gap`.

Below about `36rem` of available width the list stacks into a single column. Size it with `--param-label-width`, `--param-gap`, `--param-row-gap`, and `--param-padding`:

```css
rapi-doc {
  --param-label-width: 14rem;
  --param-padding: 0.75rem;
}
rapi-doc::part(param-name) {
  font-weight: 600;
}
rapi-doc::part(param-details) {
  color: var(--muted-foreground);
}
```

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/rapidoc/theming/css-parts/

---

# Theming Overview

> Change RapiDoc's colors, light and dark mode, corner radius, size and fonts with a few attributes and CSS variables.

RapiDoc renders inside a **Shadow DOM**, so your site's CSS (resets, Tailwind, component libraries) can't change it by accident, and its CSS can't leak into your site. You style it on purpose, in three layers:

1. **Attributes** for the common choices: theme, light or dark, corner radius, size. This page.
2. **CSS custom properties** for any color, font or size: see [Styling with CSS](/docs/rapidoc/theming/css-parts/).
3. **`::part()` selectors** for individual elements: also on [Styling with CSS](/docs/rapidoc/theming/css-parts/).

> **Note: Upgrading from RapiDoc v10?**
> RapiDoc v11 replaced styling attributes such as `bg-color`, `text-color`, `header-color`, `regular-font` and `nav-*` with CSS custom properties and `::part()` selectors. (`primary-color` still works, as a shortcut for `theme="#hex"`.) The [v10 to v11 guide](/docs/rapidoc/migration/v10-to-v11/) maps each one.

---

## 1. Attributes

Five attributes cover most visual changes. Try them:

<ThemeDemo />

### Reference

| Attribute          | Allowed Values                                                                                             | Default     | Description                                                                                                            |
| :----------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :---------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `theme`            | `ember`, `carbon`, `cobalt`, `jade`, `indigo`, `amber`, or any `#hex` code                                                | `"amber"`   | Brand color preset (dark and light palette), or a custom brand color hex code.                                        |
| `color-scheme`     | `dark`, `light`, `system`, `auto`                                                                          | `"dark"`    | Light or dark surfaces. `system` follows the operating system; `auto` follows the host page's CSS `color-scheme`, else the operating system. |
| `radius`           | `none`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `full`                                                                           | `"sm"`      | Corner radius scale applied across cards, buttons, badges, inputs, and modal dialogs.                                  |
| `scale`            | `sm`, `default`, `lg`                                                                                      | `"default"` | Proportional scale factor for UI base dimensions, body typography, code blocks, and sidebar width.                     |
| `nav-item-spacing` | `compact`, `default`, `relaxed`                                                                            | `"default"` | Vertical density and padding of sidebar navigation links, decoupled from font size scaling.                            |

---

## 2. Your brand color

Pass a hex color as the `theme`:

```html
<rapi-doc spec-url="https://api.example.com/openapi.json" theme="#2563eb" color-scheme="dark" radius="md"></rapi-doc>
```

RapiDoc then:

1. **Primary Token**: Sets `--primary` to your exact hex color.
2. **Focus Ring**: Sets `--ring` to match the brand color.
3. **Text on the color**: Sets `--primary-foreground` to black for a light brand color or white for a dark one (by YIQ luminance), so button and badge labels stay readable.

---

## 3. Radius, scale and sidebar density

### Corner Radius (`radius`)

The `radius` attribute controls roundness across the entire documentation interface:

- `radius="none"`: Sharp 0px corners for brutalist or dense terminal-style layouts.
- `radius="sm"` _(default)_: Subtle 4px (0.25rem) radius for clean, modern interfaces.
- `radius="md"`: Balanced 6px (0.375rem) radius matching contemporary web apps.
- `radius="lg"`: Pronounced 8px (0.5rem) radius for playful, consumer-facing portals.
- `radius="full"`: Pill-shaped buttons and inputs (9999px) with rounded 8px cards.

### Scaling Factor (`scale`)

The `scale` attribute controls typography, base sizing, and proportional margins:

- `scale="sm"`: Compact scale (13px base font, 17rem sidebar width). Ideal for embedded documentation cards or split-screen consoles.
- `scale="default"` _(default)_: Standard desktop scale (14px base font, 18.75rem sidebar width). Optimal for full-page documentation portals.
- `scale="lg"`: Generous scale (16px base font, 21rem sidebar width). Optimal for large monitors, accessibility compliance, and presentations.

### Sidebar Item Density (`nav-item-spacing`)

Adjust sidebar link density without altering the global font size:

- `nav-item-spacing="compact"`: 5px vertical padding for large APIs with hundreds of endpoints.
- `nav-item-spacing="default"` _(default)_: 7px vertical padding for balanced readability.
- `nav-item-spacing="relaxed"`: 10px vertical padding for touchscreens and clean navigation.

---

## 4. Fonts

RapiDoc does not download any fonts. Out of the box it uses the operating system's own UI font: San Francisco on macOS and iOS, Segoe UI on Windows, Roboto on ChromeOS and Android. That means no font requests, no third-party calls, and it works offline and under a strict Content Security Policy.

To use your brand font, load it in your page and point two CSS variables at it:

- `--font-sans`: body text, headings, and navigation links. `--heading-font` follows it unless you set that too.
- `--font-mono`: code blocks, HTTP methods, paths, and schemas.

Keep the system fonts at the end of the list, so text stays readable while your font loads or if it fails to load.

> **Caution: Declare @font-face in the page, not inside RapiDoc**
> Most browsers ignore `@font-face` rules inside a shadow root, so a font declared through `css-file` or in a `<style>` injected into RapiDoc never loads. Declare fonts in the page (a `<style>`, a stylesheet, or your app's bundle). Fonts declared in the page are available inside RapiDoc's Shadow DOM.

RapiDoc uses the weights **400**, **500**, **600**, and **700**. Load all four, or a single variable font that covers them, so the browser does not substitute the nearest weight or fake a bold.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="Self-hosted (recommended)">
Put the font files next to your site (for example in `/fonts/`) and declare them with `@font-face`. Nothing is requested from another server.

```html
<head>
  <!-- Optional: start downloading the main font early -->
  <link rel="preload" href="/fonts/InterVariable.woff2" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin />

  <style>
    @font-face {
      font-family: 'Inter';
      src: url('/fonts/InterVariable.woff2') format('woff2');
      font-weight: 100 900; /* one variable file covers every weight */
      font-style: normal;
      font-display: swap;
    }
    @font-face {
      font-family: 'JetBrains Mono';
      src: url('/fonts/JetBrainsMono-Variable.woff2') format('woff2');
      font-weight: 100 800;
      font-style: normal;
      font-display: swap;
    }

    rapi-doc {
      --font-sans: 'Inter', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif;
      --font-mono: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, Menlo, Consolas, monospace;
    }
  </style>
</head>

<body>
  <rapi-doc spec-url="https://rapidocui.com/specs/petstore.yaml" theme="jade"></rapi-doc>
</body>
```
  </TabItem>

  <TabItem label="npm (Fontsource)">
With a bundler (Vite, Astro, Next.js, webpack), [Fontsource](https://fontsource.org/) packages ship the font files and the `@font-face` rules. Your build copies the files into your site, so they are self-hosted too.

```bash
npm install @fontsource-variable/inter @fontsource-variable/jetbrains-mono
```

```js
// In your app's entry file
import '@fontsource-variable/inter';
import '@fontsource-variable/jetbrains-mono';
import 'rapidoc';
```

```css
rapi-doc {
  --font-sans: 'Inter Variable', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif;
  --font-mono: 'JetBrains Mono Variable', ui-monospace, Menlo, Consolas, monospace;
}
```
  </TabItem>

  <TabItem label="Google Fonts">
The quickest setup, but every visitor's browser contacts Google's servers, which may need consent under privacy rules such as the GDPR, and your Content Security Policy must allow `fonts.googleapis.com` and `fonts.gstatic.com`.

```html
<head>
  <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com" />
  <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin />
  <link
    href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;500;600;700&family=JetBrains+Mono:wght@400;500;600;700&display=swap"
    rel="stylesheet"
  />

  <style>
    rapi-doc {
      --font-sans: 'Inter', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif;
      --font-mono: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, Menlo, Consolas, monospace;
    }
  </style>
</head>
```
  </TabItem>

  <TabItem label="Use your app's fonts">
If your site already loads its fonts and keeps them in CSS variables (Tailwind, shadcn/ui, a design system), reuse those variables:

```css
rapi-doc {
  --font-sans: var(--font-inter, sans-serif);
  --font-mono: var(--font-jetbrains, monospace);
}
```

If your site names its variables `--font-sans` and `--font-mono` too, use `inherit`. Writing `var(--font-sans)` on `rapi-doc` would refer to itself.

```css
rapi-doc {
  --font-sans: inherit;
  --font-mono: inherit;
}
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

See the [Brand Fonts example](/examples/brand-fonts) to compare the system fonts with a brand font pairing.

---

## 5. Changing the theme at runtime

All these attributes can be changed at any time, for example from your site's own theme switcher:

```javascript
const doc = document.querySelector('rapi-doc');

// Switch brand preset or custom hex color
function setBrandColor(themeValue) {
  doc.setAttribute('theme', themeValue); // e.g., 'jade' or '#2563eb'
}

// Toggle between dark and light modes
function toggleDarkMode() {
  const current = doc.getAttribute('color-scheme') || 'dark';
  doc.setAttribute('color-scheme', current === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark');
}

// Adjust corner radius dynamically
function updateRadius(radiusValue) {
  doc.setAttribute('radius', radiusValue); // 'none', 'sm', 'md', 'lg', 'full'
}

// Make everything smaller or larger
function setScale(size) {
  doc.setAttribute('scale', size); // 'sm', 'default', 'lg'
}
```

  </DocsCard>
</CardGrid>

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/rapidoc/theming/overview/

# Built-in Themes

> RapiDoc's six built-in themes (Ember, Carbon, Cobalt, Jade, Indigo, Amber), each with a dark and a light palette, plus custom brand colors and automatic OS switching.

RapiDoc ships **six themes**. Each one defines an accent and, where the theme tints its surfaces, a background and foreground for both color schemes; every other color (cards, muted text, borders, inputs) is derived from those, so a theme looks consistent in `color-scheme="dark"`, `"light"` and `"system"`.

| Theme | Accent (dark / light) | Dark surface | Character |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ember` | `#f76b39` / `#f76b39` | Neutral charcoal `#1f1f23` | Warm, high-energy |
| `carbon` | `#fafafa` / `#18181b` | Near-black `#121214` | Monochrome, terminal-like |
| `cobalt` | `#7aa2d6` / `#3a6cb0` | Grey-blue slate `#1e2530`, cards `#181e27` | Matte, understated developer portal |
| `jade` | `#00d390` / `#047857` | Slate-navy `#1d232a`, cards `#181e25` | Payments, banking, infrastructure |
| `indigo` | `#818cf8` / `#4f46e5` | Indigo-black `#0f0e1c` | SaaS and platform products |
| `amber` (default) | `#f6a821` / `#ff791a` | Slate grey `#30333c`, cards `#383b43`, sidebar `#2c2d35` | High contrast, dashboard-like |

Light mode uses a white background in every theme; the tinted themes carry their hue into the text, cards and borders.

Try them side by side on the [Themes example](/examples/themes).

---

## Ember

Orange-red accent over neutral charcoal. This is what you get without a `theme` attribute.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="Dark">
```html
<rapi-doc spec-url="https://rapidocui.com/specs/petstore.yaml" theme="ember" color-scheme="dark"></rapi-doc>
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Light">
```html
<rapi-doc spec-url="https://rapidocui.com/specs/petstore.yaml" theme="ember" color-scheme="light"></rapi-doc>
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Carbon

Monochrome. Near-black surfaces with a white accent in dark mode; black on white in light mode. Pairs well with `radius="none"`.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="Dark">
```html
<rapi-doc spec-url="https://rapidocui.com/specs/petstore.yaml" theme="carbon" color-scheme="dark" radius="none"></rapi-doc>
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Light">
```html
<rapi-doc spec-url="https://rapidocui.com/specs/petstore.yaml" theme="carbon" color-scheme="light" radius="none"></rapi-doc>
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Cobalt

Matte steel-blue accent over grey-blue slate, with cards a shade darker than the page; muted blue accent and slate text in light mode.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="Dark">
```html
<rapi-doc spec-url="https://rapidocui.com/specs/petstore.yaml" theme="cobalt" color-scheme="dark" radius="md"></rapi-doc>
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Light">
```html
<rapi-doc spec-url="https://rapidocui.com/specs/petstore.yaml" theme="cobalt" color-scheme="light" radius="md"></rapi-doc>
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Jade

Green accent over slate-navy surfaces, with cards and code a shade darker than the page (the daisyUI look); deep green text in light mode.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="Dark">
```html
<rapi-doc spec-url="https://rapidocui.com/specs/petstore.yaml" theme="jade" color-scheme="dark"></rapi-doc>
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Light">
```html
<rapi-doc spec-url="https://rapidocui.com/specs/petstore.yaml" theme="jade" color-scheme="light"></rapi-doc>
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Indigo

Indigo accent over indigo-black surfaces; navy-violet text in light mode.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="Dark">
```html
<rapi-doc spec-url="https://rapidocui.com/specs/petstore.yaml" theme="indigo" color-scheme="dark" radius="lg"></rapi-doc>
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Light">
```html
<rapi-doc spec-url="https://rapidocui.com/specs/petstore.yaml" theme="indigo" color-scheme="light" radius="lg"></rapi-doc>
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Amber (default)

Amber accent over slate grey, with lighter cards, a darker sidebar and white headings: the brightest accent of the presets, for a high-contrast look. In light mode the accent is the orange `#ff791a`.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="Dark">
```html
<rapi-doc spec-url="https://rapidocui.com/specs/petstore.yaml" theme="amber" color-scheme="dark" radius="md"></rapi-doc>
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Light">
```html
<rapi-doc spec-url="https://rapidocui.com/specs/petstore.yaml" theme="amber" color-scheme="light" radius="md"></rapi-doc>
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

---

## Custom brand color

Pass a hex code as the `theme`. RapiDoc sets `--primary` and `--ring` to it and picks black or white for `--primary-foreground` by luminance, over neutral charcoal surfaces (as Ember).

```html
<rapi-doc spec-url="https://rapidocui.com/specs/petstore.yaml" theme="#2563eb" color-scheme="dark" radius="md"></rapi-doc>
```

To change more than the accent, set the CSS variables on the element; see [Theming Overview](/docs/rapidoc/theming/overview/).

```css
rapi-doc {
  --background: #0b1220;
  --foreground: #e2e8f0;
}
```

---

## Follow the operating system

`color-scheme="system"` switches between the theme's dark and light palette with the OS preference. `color-scheme="auto"` follows the host page's CSS `color-scheme` instead (as set, for example, by a site's own light/dark switch), and falls back to the OS preference.

```html
<rapi-doc spec-url="https://rapidocui.com/specs/petstore.yaml" theme="jade" color-scheme="system"></rapi-doc>
```

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/rapidoc/theming/prebuilt-themes/
