## Which package do I need?

RapiDoc is a family of packages. Most sites need only the first one, `rapidoc`, which is a browser bundle you load with a `<script>` tag. The others are Node packages for build steps, local tooling and full developer portals.

### In the browser

`rapidoc` has no runtime dependencies: everything it needs is bundled into its JavaScript files.

| Import | Elements | What it is for |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `rapidoc` (`dist/rapidoc-min.js`) | `<rapi-doc>` | The full interactive API reference: navigation, search, schemas, **Try**, authentication, [in-browser mocking](/docs/rapidoc/mocking/in-browser/) and [MCP export](/docs/mcp/). |
| | `<rapi-doc-mini>` | [One endpoint or a few](/docs/rapidoc-mini/), embedded in a blog post, tutorial or changelog. |
| | `<oauth-receiver>` | The [OAuth 2.0 callback page](/docs/rapidoc/authentication/oauth/) that hands the authorization code back to `<rapi-doc>`. |
| `rapidoc/flow` (`dist/rapidoc-flow-min.js`) | `<rapi-flow>` | [Arazzo workflows](https://flow.rapidocui.com/) drawn as a diagram and run in the browser. A separate bundle, so pages without workflows don't download it. |

```bash
npm install rapidoc
```

### In Node

| Package | What it is for |
| :--- | :--- |
| `@rapidoc/cli` | The `rapidoc` command: [preview, validate, lint and bundle](/docs/cli/) a spec, run a [mock server](https://mock.rapidocui.com/), turn a spec into an MCP server, and build and serve developer portals. |
| `@rapidoc/mock` | The [mock server](https://mock.rapidocui.com/) behind `rapidoc mock`: answers every operation over HTTP from examples or generated data, validates requests and checks OAuth tokens, and with `--stateful` keeps what you create. Also usable as a library. |
| `@rapidoc/mcp` | Turns OpenAPI and Arazzo specs into [MCP tools](/docs/mcp/server/#in-node-rapidocmcp): manifest builder, runtime and server project writer. The same code `<rapi-doc>` uses in the browser. |
| `@rapidoc/embed` | The shared core of integrations (plugins and middleware for frameworks, docs sites and tools): renders the standard host page for `<rapi-doc>` and lists the routes to serve. See [Build an Integration](/docs/integrations/build-your-own/). |
| `@rapidoc/hono` | Serves the API reference from a [Hono](https://hono.dev) app: `app.use(rapidoc({ specUrl }))`. See [Server frameworks](/docs/integrations/node/). |
| `@rapidoc/express`, `@rapidoc/fastify` | The same for [Express](https://expressjs.com) and [Fastify](https://fastify.dev) apps. See [Server frameworks](/docs/integrations/node/). |
| `@rapidoc/vitepress` | Adds API reference pages to a [VitePress](https://vitepress.dev) site, in its theme and sidebar. See [Documentation sites](/docs/integrations/docs-sites/). |
| `@rapidoc/docusaurus` | Adds API reference pages to a [Docusaurus](https://docusaurus.io) site, in its theme and sidebar. See [Documentation sites](/docs/integrations/docs-sites/). |
| `@rapidoc/starlight` | Adds API reference pages to a [Starlight](https://starlight.astro.build) site, in its layout and sidebar. See [Documentation sites](/docs/integrations/docs-sites/). |
| `@rapidoc/prerender` | Renders `<rapi-doc>` to HTML at build time (Declarative Shadow DOM or light DOM), plus a static sidebar and Arazzo diagrams as SVG. Good for SEO and first paint. See [Pre-rendering](/docs/prerender/). |

### Developer portals

A developer portal puts your API references next to Markdown guides, with search, navigation and optional single sign-on (SSO) through Okta, Microsoft Entra ID or any OpenID Connect provider. These packages are documented in the [RapiDoc Portal docs](https://portal.rapidocui.com/); for private portals, see [SSO and access](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/access/overview/).

| Package | What it is for |
| :--- | :--- |
| `create-rapidoc` | Scaffolds a new portal: `npm create rapidoc`. `rapidoc init` does the same. |
| `@rapidoc/portal` | The portal engine behind `rapidoc dev` and `rapidoc build`: OpenAPI specs and Markdown, MDX or Markdoc guides in, a static site out. |
| `@rapidoc/server` | Serves a built portal with single sign-on (OpenID Connect) and per-page access rules (`rapidoc serve`). |

### Which do I need?

- **An API reference on a page you already have**: `rapidoc`. Start with the [Quickstart](/docs/rapidoc/get-started/quickstart/).
- **A mock API your frontend or tests can call**: `@rapidoc/cli` and `@rapidoc/mock`.
- **An MCP server for AI agents**: the Export button in `<rapi-doc>`, `rapidoc mcp`, or `@rapidoc/mcp` in your own code.
- **Static HTML of your reference at build time**: `@rapidoc/prerender`.
- **An API reference served by your Hono app**: `@rapidoc/hono`.
- **An API reference inside your Starlight docs**: `@rapidoc/starlight`.
- **A RapiDoc plugin for another framework or tool**: `@rapidoc/embed`.
- **A whole developer portal**: `create-rapidoc`, which installs `@rapidoc/cli` and `@rapidoc/portal`.

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/

---

# RapiDoc Mini

> Embed one endpoint, or a few, with its Try console in a blog post, tutorial or changelog, using <rapi-doc-mini>.

`<rapi-doc>` is a whole API reference with navigation and search. `<rapi-doc-mini>` shows only the operations you pick, with their parameters, schemas and **Try** console, so you can put a working endpoint in the middle of a tutorial, changelog or wiki page without an `<iframe>`. It is in the same bundle as `<rapi-doc>`.

> **Tip:**
> See it running on the [RapiDoc Mini page](/rapidoc-mini/).

## Show one endpoint

Point `spec-url` at your spec and choose operations with `filter-operations`:

```html
<script type="module" src="https://unpkg.com/rapidoc/dist/rapidoc-min.js"></script>

<rapi-doc-mini
  spec-url="https://rapidocui.com/specs/petstore.yaml"
  filter-operations="GET /pet/{petId}"
></rapi-doc-mini>
```

## Choose operations

`filter-operations` is a list of terms, separated by spaces or commas. An operation is shown when it matches any term (every operation is, when there is none) and no term that starts with `!`.

| Term | Shows |
| :--- | :--- |
| `getPetById` | The operation with that `operationId` (exact, case-sensitive). |
| `GET /pet/{petId}` | That method and path. |
| `/pet/{petId}` | Every method on that path. |
| `/pet/*`, `/pet/**` | Paths matching the glob: `*` is one path segment, `**` any number of segments, `/pet` itself included. |
| `tag:store` | Operations with that tag. Quote a name with spaces: `tag:"Pet Store"`. |
| `badge:Beta` | Operations with that `x-badges` label, or an OpenAPI 3.2 tag of `kind: badge` (by its label or name). |
| `deprecated` | Deprecated operations. |
| `!<term>` | Leaves out what the term matches, as in `!badge:Internal` or `!deprecated`. |

Methods, paths, tags and badge labels are compared without case. Paths are matched whole, never as part of a longer path: `POST /user` does not show `POST /user/createWithList`; use `/user/**` for everything under `/user`.

An `operationId` is matched only when the term is none of the other kinds: an id that starts with `tag:` or `badge:`, or is the word `deprecated`, is read as that kind instead. Select such an operation by its method and path (`GET /path`).

`allow-try` takes the same terms, to turn **Try** on only for the operations they select: `allow-try="!deprecated !tag:pending-implementation"`. The operations they leave out keep their request documentation and show a disabled **TRY DISABLED** button.

The operations are shown in the order of the first term they match, so a list of operationIds keeps its order, unless `sort-endpoints-by` is set:

```html
<rapi-doc-mini
  spec-url="https://rapidocui.com/specs/petstore.yaml"
  filter-operations="placeOrder getOrderById"
></rapi-doc-mini>

<!-- Everything tagged store, except the delete -->
<rapi-doc-mini
  spec-url="https://rapidocui.com/specs/petstore.yaml"
  filter-operations="tag:store !DELETE /store/order/{orderId}"
></rapi-doc-mini>
```

## More

[Recipes](/docs/rapidoc-mini/recipes/): several endpoints, an expanded layout, endpoints from two APIs, an API key, showing an operation from a script, and a mini next to a workflow.

## Attributes

Every attribute, method and event, grouped by what it changes, is on the [`<rapi-doc-mini>` API reference](/docs/rapidoc-mini/reference/), read from the element's source.

## `<rapi-doc>` or `<rapi-doc-mini>`?

<RapidocMiniComparisonTable docs />

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/rapidoc-mini/

---

# Recipes

> Ways to use <rapi-doc-mini> - several endpoints, an expanded layout, endpoints from two APIs, an API key, an operation shown from a script, and a mini next to an Arazzo workflow.

How to pick operations is on the [overview](/docs/rapidoc-mini/#choose-operations); these are common ways to put them on a page.

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="Several endpoints">
    ```html
    <rapi-doc-mini
      spec-url="/specs/reqres.yaml"
      filter-operations="GET /users/{userId} POST /users"
      schema-style="table"
    ></rapi-doc-mini>
    ```
  </TabItem>

  <TabItem label="Always expanded">
    ```html
    <rapi-doc-mini
      spec-url="/specs/reqres.yaml"
      filter-operations="POST /users"
      paths-expanded="true"
      layout="column"
    ></rapi-doc-mini>
    ```
  </TabItem>

  <TabItem label="Endpoints from two APIs">
    Each element loads its own OpenAPI spec, so one page can walk through a flow that spans services:

    ```html
    <rapi-doc-mini spec-url="https://api.example.com/auth/openapi.yaml" filter-operations="POST /oauth/token"></rapi-doc-mini>
    <rapi-doc-mini spec-url="https://api.example.com/billing/openapi.yaml" filter-operations="POST /charges"></rapi-doc-mini>
    ```
  </TabItem>

  <TabItem label="With an API key">
    The key is sent with every **Try** request when all three `api-key-*` attributes are set:

    ```html
    <rapi-doc-mini
      spec-url="/specs/api.yaml"
      filter-operations="GET /orders"
      api-key-name="X-API-Key"
      api-key-location="header"
      api-key-value="test-key-123"
    ></rapi-doc-mini>
    ```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

If the spec can't be loaded, the element renders nothing and logs the error to the browser console.

## Show an operation from a script

`showOperation(operation)` expands one operation and scrolls it into view. Pass its `operationId` or its method and path; it resolves to `false` when the element does not show that operation (the spec is not loaded yet, or `filter-operations` leaves it out).

```js
await document.querySelector('rapi-doc-mini').showOperation('GET /pet/{petId}');
```

## Next to a workflow

[`<rapi-flow>`](https://flow.rapidocui.com/docs/pairing/#one-element-per-api) pairs with one `<rapi-doc-mini>` per API its Arazzo workflow calls. Name the API with `arazzo-source`; `<rapi-flow>` then sets the mini's `filter-operations` to the workflow's calls to that API, in step order, and clicking a step shows its operation in the mini.

```html
<rapi-flow arazzo-url="/workflows/ship-a-parcel.arazzo.yaml" for="rates-api shipments-api"></rapi-flow>
<rapi-doc-mini id="rates-api" arazzo-source="rates" spec-url="/specs/rates.yaml"></rapi-doc-mini>
<rapi-doc-mini id="shipments-api" arazzo-source="shipments" spec-url="/specs/shipments.yaml"></rapi-doc-mini>
```

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/rapidoc-mini/recipes/

---

```js
const mini = document.querySelector('rapi-doc-mini');

```

# RapiPdf

> Turn an OpenAPI 3.x or Swagger 2.0 spec into a PDF reference in the browser with the <rapi-pdf> element, and choose what goes in it.

`<rapi-pdf>` is a spec URL field and a button that turns an OpenAPI 3.x or Swagger 2.0 spec into a PDF: a cover page, a table of contents, the security schemes, and every operation with its parameters, request bodies and responses. It runs in the browser; [`rapipdf/node`](/docs/rapipdf/node/) and [`rapidoc pdf`](/docs/cli/pdf/) make the same PDF in Node and on the command line. [Try it](/rapipdf/#demo).

## Add it to a page

<Tabs>
  <TabItem label="Script tag">
```html
<script src="https://unpkg.com/rapipdf/dist/rapipdf-min.js"></script>

<rapi-pdf spec-url="https://rapidocui.com/specs/petstore.yaml"></rapi-pdf>
```
  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Bundler">
```bash
npm install rapipdf
```

```javascript
import 'rapipdf';
```
  </TabItem>
</Tabs>

`rapipdf-min.js` is a classic script with everything in it, so `<script src>` works with or without `type="module"`. With a bundler, `import 'rapipdf'` loads `dist/rapipdf.js`: a few kilobytes that fetch the PDF generator (spec parser, pdfmake and its fonts, about two megabytes) the first time a PDF is asked for.

The reader presses the button, or Enter in the field. The PDF opens in a new tab; with `output="download"` it is saved instead, as `file-name`. If the browser blocks the new tab, the PDF is downloaded. While a PDF is being made the element has the `generating` attribute and its button is disabled.

## Choose what goes in the PDF

```html
<rapi-pdf
  spec-url="/openapi.yaml"
  pdf-title="Orders API"
  pdf-footer-text="© Example Corp"
  pdf-schema-style="table"
  include-example="true"
  include-api-list="true"
  pdf-primary-color="#0b5394"
></rapi-pdf>
```

- **Sections**: `include-info` (the cover page), `include-toc`, `include-security` and `include-api-details` (the operations) are on by default; `false` leaves one out. `include-example` adds request and response examples, and `include-api-list` a closing list of every operation.
- **Order**: tags are sorted by name; `pdf-sort-tags="false"` keeps the spec's order.
- **Look**: `pdf-title`, `pdf-footer-text`, `pdf-schema-style` (`object` or `table`), `pdf-primary-color` and `pdf-alternate-color`.
- **The element itself**: `button-label`, `button-bg`, `button-color`, `input-bg`, `input-color`, and `hide-input="true"` for a button alone.

Every attribute, with its default, is in the [API reference](/docs/rapipdf/reference/).

## Make it from a script

```javascript
const pdf = document.querySelector('rapi-pdf');

await pdf.generatePdf();               // open or download, as `output` says
await pdf.generatePdf(specObject);     // a spec object or spec text instead of spec-url
const blob = await pdf.getPdfBlob();   // the PDF itself: show it, upload it

pdf.addEventListener('pdf-generated', (e) => console.log(e.detail.output));
pdf.addEventListener('pdf-error', (e) => console.error(e.detail.error));
```

`getPdfBlob()` opens and downloads nothing, for a page that shows the PDF itself or where new tabs are not allowed.

## Labels in another language

The words printed in the PDF ("REQUEST", "RESPONSE", "Parameters", …) come from a table of labels. Replace any of them with JSON in a `<template>`, the element's first child:

```html
<rapi-pdf spec-url="/openapi.yaml">
  <template>
    { "request": "ANFRAGE", "response": "ANTWORT", "parameters": "Parameter" }
  </template>
</rapi-pdf>
```

The keys are those of `DEFAULT_LOCALIZE`, exported by `rapipdf/node`. For text the built-in Roboto font has no glyphs for, such as Chinese, Japanese or Korean, make the PDF [in Node](/docs/rapipdf/node/#your-own-fonts) or [with the CLI](/docs/cli/pdf/) with your own font.

> **Note:**
> The browser fetches the spec, so a spec on another server must allow cross-origin requests.

<CardGrid>
  <LinkCard title="In Node" href="/docs/rapipdf/node/" description="generatePdf() returns the same PDF as a Buffer, for a build step." />
  <LinkCard title="API Reference" href="/docs/rapipdf/reference/" description="Every attribute, method and event of <rapi-pdf>." />
</CardGrid>

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/rapipdf/

---

# RapiPdf in Node

> Make the RapiPdf PDF of an OpenAPI spec in Node with generatePdf() of rapipdf/node, for a build step that publishes it next to your docs.

`rapipdf/node` makes the same PDF as `<rapi-pdf>`, from a file, a URL, spec text or a spec object, and returns it as a Buffer. Use it in a build step that publishes the PDF next to your docs; [`rapidoc pdf`](/docs/cli/pdf/) runs it from the command line.

```bash
npm install rapipdf
```

```javascript title="make-pdf.mjs"
import { writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { generatePdf } from 'rapipdf/node';

const pdf = await generatePdf('openapi.yaml', {
  pdfTitle: 'Orders API',
  pdfSchemaStyle: 'table',
  includeExample: true,
});
await writeFile('dist/reference.pdf', pdf);
```

`$ref`s to other files are followed, and Swagger 2.0 is converted to OpenAPI 3. `generatePdf` rejects when the spec can't be loaded.

## Options

Each option is an attribute of the element, in camelCase: `pdf-title` is `pdfTitle`, `include-example` is `includeExample` (a boolean here, not a string).

| Option | Default | |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `pdfTitle` | `"API Reference"` | Title on the cover page. |
| `pdfFooterText` | | Text at the bottom left of every page. |
| `pdfSchemaStyle` | `"object"` | Schemas as an indented object tree, or `"table"`. |
| `pdfPrimaryColor` | `#b44646` | Color of headings and operation titles. |
| `pdfAlternateColor` | `#005b96` | Color of section labels and table headers. |
| `pdfSortTags` | `true` | Sort the tags by name. |
| `includeInfo` | `true` | The cover page with the API's title, version, description and contact. |
| `includeToc` | `true` | The table of contents. |
| `includeSecurity` | `true` | The security schemes. |
| `includeApiDetails` | `true` | The operations, with parameters, request bodies and responses. |
| `includeExample` | `false` | Request and response examples. |
| `includeApiList` | `false` | A closing list of every operation, by tag. |
| `localize` | | Labels to replace, keyed as in `DEFAULT_LOCALIZE`. |

## Your own fonts

The PDF uses Roboto and Roboto Mono. For text they have no glyphs for, such as Chinese, Japanese or Korean, pass TrueType or OpenType files:

```javascript
const pdf = await generatePdf('openapi.yaml', {
  font: './fonts/NotoSansJP-Regular.ttf',
  monoFont: './fonts/NotoSansMonoCJKjp-Regular.otf',
  localize: { request: 'リクエスト', response: 'レスポンス' },
});
```

## The steps on their own

`generatePdf` is three steps, each exported: `loadSpecFile(spec)` loads a spec and resolves every `$ref`; `buildDocDefinition(spec, options)` turns it into a [pdfmake](https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/) document definition, with no file or network access; `renderPdf(docDefinition, { font, monoFont })` renders that to a PDF. Change the document definition between the last two steps to add a page or a logo. The types are in `rapipdf/node`'s `node.d.ts`.

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/rapipdf/node/

---

# RapiDoc CLI

> The rapidoc command (@rapidoc/cli) previews, validates, lints and bundles OpenAPI specs, writes them as PDFs, mocks them and turns them into MCP servers.

`@rapidoc/cli` gives you the `rapidoc` command. It builds and runs [developer portals](https://portal.rapidocui.com/), and the commands in this section also work on plain OpenAPI files, wherever you use `<rapi-doc>`.

```bash
npm install -D @rapidoc/cli
npx rapidoc --help            # every command
npx rapidoc validate --help   # one command's options and examples
```

## The commands

| Command | What it does |
| :--- | :--- |
| [`preview`](/docs/cli/preview/) | Shows a spec in `<rapi-doc>` and reloads it as you edit. |
| [`validate`](/docs/cli/validate/) | Checks a spec strictly against the OpenAPI Specification. |
| [`lint`](/docs/cli/lint/) | Checks what a good reference needs, beyond validity. |
| [`bundle`](/docs/cli/bundle/) | Joins a spec split over files into one document. |
| [`pdf`](/docs/cli/pdf/) | Writes the reference as a PDF. |
| [`mock`](/docs/cli/mock/) | Serves the API with example or generated responses. |
| [`mcp`](/docs/cli/mcp/) | Turns the spec into an MCP server for AI agents. |

## Everything else

`rapidoc doctor` checks your setup (Node, package versions) and prints a report for bug reports. The other commands (`init`, `dev`, `build`, `serve`, `migrate`) create and run a developer portal: OpenAPI references next to Markdown and Markdoc guides, with search and optional [single sign-on](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/access/overview/). [All Commands & Options](/docs/cli/reference/) lists every command and option; the portal commands are explained in the [RapiDoc Portal docs](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/reference/cli/).

In a terminal, `rapidoc` asks for what the options don't say and shows a menu when run alone; piped, in CI or with `--yes` it never asks. Exit codes: `0` success, `1` problems in the input, `2` a wrong command line. `rapidoc completion zsh|bash|fish` prints a completion script for commands, options and their values.

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/cli/

---

# rapidoc bundle

> Join an OpenAPI spec split over several files into one document, or dereference it, for tools that can't follow $refs to other files.

```bash
npx rapidoc bundle openapi.yaml -o dist/openapi.json
npx rapidoc bundle openapi.yaml > openapi.bundled.yaml
npx rapidoc bundle openapi.yaml --dereference > flat.yaml
npx rapidoc bundle --api orders -o dist/orders.yaml   # an API of a portal's rapidoc.config.*
```

`rapidoc bundle` loads a spec and every file its `$ref`s reach, and writes one document. `<rapi-doc>` and the portal follow `$ref`s across files, so they don't need this; code generators, gateways and review tools often do.

## What it writes

Every `$ref` to another file becomes a **component**, holding a copy of what it pointed to, and the `$ref` is rewritten to point there. `$ref`s within the main file stay as they are.

```yaml title="specs/orders.yaml (before)"
schema:
  $ref: "./schemas/Order.yaml"
```

```yaml title="dist/orders.yaml (after)"
schema:
  $ref: "#/components/schemas/Order"
# ...
components:
  schemas:
    Order:
      type: object
      # ... from schemas/Order.yaml, its own $refs rewritten the same way
```

- The component goes where the `$ref` is written: a schema under `components/schemas`, a parameter under `components/parameters`, and so on for responses, request bodies, headers, examples, links, callbacks and (OpenAPI 3.1) path items. In Swagger 2.0 they go under `definitions`, `parameters` and `responses`.
- The name is the file's name (`Order.yaml` → `Order`) or, for `file.yaml#/NotFound`, the last part of the pointer. The same target referenced from several places is copied once. A name already taken by something else gets `-2`, `-3`.
- A `$ref` where the kind can't be told (under a vendor extension, say) is inlined.
- Keys keep their order; comments are not kept (the output is data).

Before writing, the result is checked against the OpenAPI Specification, like [`rapidoc validate`](/docs/cli/validate/) does. If it fails, nothing is written and the errors are listed (run `validate` on the source for file, line and column).

## Options

| Option | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| `-o, --output <file>` | Write here, as JSON or YAML by the extension; folders are created. Without it the document goes to stdout (YAML). |
| `--format yaml \| json` | The output format, when the extension shouldn't decide (or for stdout). |
| `--dereference` | Inline every `$ref`, in-file ones too, so the output has none. A recursive schema can't be inlined: the command stops and names the cycle. |
| `--no-validate` | Write the result without checking it against the specification. |
| `--remote` | Also fetch remote `$ref`s. Without it they are left as they are, with a warning. |
| `--api <id>` | Bundle the spec of this API from `rapidoc.config.*` (its default version) instead of a file. Needs `@rapidoc/portal`. |

Exit code `1` when a `$ref` points to nothing (reported with file, line and column), when the result isn't valid OpenAPI, or when `--dereference` meets a cycle; nothing is written in those cases.

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/cli/bundle/

---

# rapidoc lint

> Check that a valid OpenAPI spec also makes a good reference: operationIds, summaries, examples, declared tags and security.

```bash
npx rapidoc lint openapi.yaml             # one file (or a URL)
npx rapidoc lint openapi.yaml --rule operation-description=warn --strict
npx rapidoc lint                          # in a portal: every API in rapidoc.config.*
```

A valid spec can still make a poor reference: operations without an `operationId` get anchors that change when their summary is edited, bodies without examples leave **Try** and the mock server with nothing to show, tags that aren't declared have no description for their sidebar group. `rapidoc lint` finds those. It runs [`validate`](/docs/cli/validate/)'s check first, so one CI step covers both; an invalid spec is not linted further.

Each finding names the file, line and column, and the rule:

```text
🔍 orders: specs/orders.yaml
   ❌ 1 error(s):
      specs/orders.yaml:37:7  operationId "createOrder" is also used by POST /orders  [operation-operationId-unique]  (#/paths/~1orders~1{id}/delete/operationId)
   ⚠️ specs/orders.yaml:11:5  GET /orders has no summary  [operation-summary]  (#/paths/~1orders/get)
   ⚠️ specs/orders.yaml:22:11  application/json request body has no example  [media-example]  (#/paths/~1orders/post/requestBody/content/application~1json)
```

## Rules

Each rule has a severity: `error` fails the run, `warn` is reported (and fails with `--strict`), `off` is skipped. The defaults lean on `warn`, so the first run on an existing spec doesn't fail CI. `rapidoc lint --rules` prints this list.

| Rule | Checks | Why it matters | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `operation-operationId` | Every operation has an `operationId`. | Anchors and page URLs are built from it (otherwise from the summary, which changes); so are MCP tool names. | warn |
| `operation-operationId-unique` | No two operations share one. | They would share an anchor and a tool name. | error |
| `operation-operationId-url-safe` | Letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.` only. | It appears in URLs. | warn |
| `operation-summary` | Every operation has a summary. | The sidebar label and the MCP tool's title. | warn |
| `operation-description` | Every operation has a description. | Readers, and the MCP tool's description. | off |
| `parameter-description` | Every parameter has a description. A `$ref` is checked where the parameter is written. | The reference shows it beside the field; an AI agent calling the API through MCP has nothing else to go on. | warn |
| `operation-tag-defined` | Tags used are in the top-level `tags` list. | The sidebar group's description and order come from there. | warn |
| `tag-description` | Every top-level tag has a description. | It introduces the group. | off |
| `operation-2xx-response` | A 2xx or 3xx response is documented. | Try has nothing to show as the expected result. | warn |
| `operation-4xx-response` | A 4xx response is documented. | Readers see the error shapes. | off |
| `response-error-schema` | A 4xx or 5xx response that says what went wrong has a schema. 401, 403, 404, 405, 406, 410, 412 and 429 may go without. | Clients read the error from it; the mock server answers `Prefer: code=400` with a body of that shape. | warn |
| `security-defined` | POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE have a security requirement, their own or the document's. `security: []` opts out. | Try and the mock server need it; MCP marks them as consequential. | warn |
| `security-scheme-defined` | Every scheme a requirement names is declared. | Try's authentication panel is built from the declarations. | error |
| `no-unused-components` | Every component is referenced. | Documentation of nothing. | warn |
| `media-example` | Request and response bodies have an example, on the media type or its schema (or on every property). | Try fills the request with it; the mock server answers with it. | warn |
| `example-named-map` | A media type's `example` is the value itself, not a map of named examples (`example: { "Calendar": { ... } }`), which belongs under `examples`. | Try and the mock server would send the map, name included. | warn |
| `example-matches-schema` | Request and response examples fit their schema. Needs `@rapidoc/mock` installed; without it the rule is skipped and lint says so. | Try sends them and the mock server answers with them. | warn |
| `schema-oneof-discriminator` | A `oneOf` or `anyOf` between object schemas has a `discriminator`, or a property with a different fixed value (`const`, or an `enum` of one) in each. | A client, a code generator and the mock server otherwise guess the shape. | warn |
| `path-kebab-case` | Path segments other than parameters are kebab-case. | Naming. | off |
| `no-server-example-com` | Servers aren't example.com or localhost. | Try would call nowhere. | warn |
| `info-contact` | `info.contact` is set. | Shown in the reference's header. | off |
| `info-license` | `info.license` is set. | Shown in the reference's header. | off |

## Rules for the stateful mock

`rapidoc mock --stateful` works out resources, keys and links from the spec. Where the spec leaves that unclear, the mock assumes something or keeps no state for the operation. `--stateful` reports those places, before you run the mock:

```bash
npx rapidoc lint openapi.yaml --stateful
```

```
   ⚠️ openapi.yaml:12:5  GET /pets: query parameter color matches no field of Pet: the mock ignores it when listing  [stateful-list-filter]
   ⚠️ openapi.yaml:163:5  Resource Widget: no key field found for {code}: the mock can't tell one record from another, so reads, updates and deletes of one record keep no state  [stateful-resource-key]
```

These rules are `off` by default. `--stateful` turns on the first six as warnings; a severity you set by name (`--rule`, or the config) wins. The findings are the mock's own, the same as the **Needs review** labels of its [Mock UI](https://mock.rapidocui.com/), so they need `@rapidoc/mock` installed.

Lint reads the [`mock.config.yaml`](https://mock.rapidocui.com/) beside the spec (or the one `--mock-config` names), the file where you correct what the mock worked out. What it states is not reported, so the list shrinks as you settle things: a resource whose `key` you set, an operation you gave an `action`. An entry in it that no longer fits the spec is reported as `mock-config`, with the file's name.

| Rule | It reports | What to do |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `stateful-resource-key` | A resource whose key the spec doesn't show: no path parameter matches a field, or there is no item path such as `/things/{id}`. | Name the path parameter after the field (`{petId}` and `id`), or add the field. |
| `stateful-list-filter` | A query parameter of a list that matches no field of what it returns (paging and sorting parameters are fine). | Name it after the field it filters by. Otherwise the mock ignores it. |
| `stateful-write-unmapped` | A `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE` that fits no resource. | Nothing, if it is an action and not a change to a record; the mock answers it without changing data. |
| `stateful-reference-target` | A field that looks like a reference (`owner_id`) to a resource the spec doesn't have. | Nothing, if the other resource lives in another API; the mock fills the field with generated values. |
| `stateful-response-unnamed` | A collection and its item path whose records are described by an inline schema. | Move the schema under `components.schemas` and refer to it: the mock knows a record by its schema's name. |
| `stateful-operation-assumed` | Another assumption about what an operation does: a `GET` that returns a different schema, a `POST` on an item path. | Check the assumption in the message. |
| `stateful-relation-assumed` | A link between resources matched by more than the field's plain name (`active_credential_id` to `Credential`). Not turned on by `--stateful`: these are usually right. | Turn it on by name to review them. |

## Settings

Set severities in `rapidoc.config.yaml`: in the folder you run the command from, or in the folder you pass it. Most specific wins: `--rule` on the command line, then the API's entry under `lint.apis` (in a portal), then `lint.rules`, then the defaults above.

```yaml title="rapidoc.config.yaml"
lint:
  rules:
    operation-description: warn
    no-unused-components: off
  apis:
    legacy: # a portal API that can't meet a rule yet
      operation-operationId: off
```

The `lint` key is read straight from the file, so linting one spec needs no other package. A misspelled rule name is an error with a suggestion.

## Options

| Option | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| `--rule <name>=<error \| warn \| off>` | Set a rule's severity; repeat for more. |
| `--rules` | List the rules, their defaults and what they check. |
| `--stateful` | Also report what the stateful mock had to assume or could not map (the `stateful-*` rules). Needs `@rapidoc/mock`. |
| `--mock-config <file>` | With the `stateful-*` rules: your corrections for the stateful mock. Default: `mock.config.yaml` beside the spec or in the folder. |
| `--format pretty \| json \| sarif` | `pretty` (default) for the terminal; `json` for scripts; `sarif` for GitHub code scanning, with every rule described. |
| `--strict` | Fail on warnings too. |
| `--remote` | Also fetch remote `$ref`s (and, in a portal, remote specs in `apis:`). |

## In CI

Exit code `1` on errors (or warnings with `--strict`), `2` for a wrong rule name or severity:

```yaml title=".github/workflows/api.yml"
# in a job's steps:
- run: npx rapidoc lint openapi.yaml --strict
```

Upload a SARIF report to see the findings on the pull request, as [`rapidoc validate`](/docs/cli/validate/#in-ci) shows.

One spec, a URL or a folder of OpenAPI files needs `@rapidoc/cli` alone; a portal folder (with `rapidoc.config.*`) needs `@rapidoc/portal`, to read the `apis:` list.

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/cli/lint/

---

# rapidoc mcp

> Turn an OpenAPI spec into an MCP server for AI agents: export the project or serve it over stdio.

```bash
npx rapidoc mcp export openapi.yaml --out-dir orders-mcp   # the server project
npx rapidoc mcp serve openapi.yaml                         # run it over stdio, no files
```

`mcp export` writes the same project as `<rapi-doc>`'s [Export MCP Server](/docs/mcp/) button. `mcp serve` runs it directly, so an agent's config can start it with `npx rapidoc mcp serve <spec>` (it needs `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` installed). Credentials come from the environment, one variable per security scheme; `--base-url` points the calls at `rapidoc mock`, and `--arazzo` adds workflows as tools. `EXTERNAL_HOSTS` (comma-separated, `*` for any) lists the hosts a workflow step's [`x-operation`](https://flow.rapidocui.com/docs/extensions/#calls-outside-the-api-sources-x-operation) URL computed at run time may go to, besides those the workflow names.

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/cli/mcp/

---

# rapidoc mock

> Serve an API from its OpenAPI spec, with example or generated responses, request validation and token checks.

```bash
npx rapidoc mock openapi.yaml                    # http://localhost:4010/openapi
npx rapidoc mock ./specs --port 4011             # every OpenAPI file in the folder
npx rapidoc mock openapi.yaml --stateful         # keep state: creates, updates and deletes are remembered
```

`rapidoc mock` answers every operation of the spec over HTTP, from its examples or with generated data. It validates requests and can check OAuth tokens against your OpenID Connect issuer. With `--stateful` it also [keeps state](https://mock.rapidocui.com/docs/state/overview/): it works out the resources from the spec, starts with generated records, and serves a page at `/__mock/ui` to look inside. It needs `@rapidoc/mock`. See [Mock Server](https://mock.rapidocui.com/) for the options, and the [overview](/docs/rapidoc/mocking/in-browser/#in-the-page-or-as-a-server) for how it compares with the in-browser mock.

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/cli/mock/

---

# rapidoc pdf

> Write the API reference of an OpenAPI spec as a PDF, with your title, colors, fonts and labels.

```bash
npm install -D rapipdf
npx rapidoc pdf openapi.yaml
npx rapidoc pdf openapi.yaml -o dist/reference.pdf --title "Orders API" --examples
```

`rapidoc pdf` writes the API reference of a spec as a PDF: a cover page, a table of contents, the security schemes, and every operation with its parameters, request bodies and responses. The spec can be a file or a URL, OpenAPI 3.x or Swagger 2.0, and `$ref`s to other files are followed. Without `-o` the file is named after the spec (`openapi.pdf`) and written to the current folder.

- `--schema-style table` prints schemas as tables instead of indented object trees, `--examples` adds request and response examples, and `--api-list` adds a closing list of every operation.
- `--no-info`, `--no-toc`, `--no-security` and `--no-api-details` leave a section out, and `--no-sort-tags` keeps the tags in the spec's order.
- `--title`, `--footer`, `--primary-color` and `--alternate-color` set the cover title, the page footer and the two colors.
- `--labels labels.json` replaces the labels printed in the PDF ("REQUEST", "RESPONSE", …), for a PDF in another language.
- `--font file.ttf` uses your font in place of the built-in Roboto. Use it for text Roboto has no glyphs for, such as Chinese, Japanese or Korean (`--mono-font` does the same for code).

The command needs the [`rapipdf`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/rapipdf) package next to the CLI, the same package whose `<rapi-pdf>` element makes this PDF in the browser.

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/cli/pdf/

---

# rapidoc preview

> Show an OpenAPI spec in <rapi-doc> while you edit it, reloading on every change.

```bash
npx rapidoc preview openapi.yaml --open
```

Shows the spec in `<rapi-doc>` on `http://localhost:4000` and reloads it whenever a file in its folder changes, so you can edit the YAML and watch the page. Relative `$ref`s to other files work. `--theme` picks a `<rapi-doc>` theme; a URL works too (`npx rapidoc preview https://example.com/openapi.json`), without reloading.

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/cli/preview/

---

# All Commands & Options

> Every rapidoc command and option, the questions it asks, its exit codes and the packages each command needs.

```bash
rapidoc <command> [options]
```

The command comes from the npm package `@rapidoc/cli`. In a project that has it installed, run it as `npx rapidoc <command>` or through the `npm run` scripts. Without it, run `npx @rapidoc/cli <command>`: `npx rapidoc` would look for the npm package `rapidoc`, the `<rapi-doc>` web component, which has no command.

| Command | Does |
| :--- | :--- |
| `init [dir]` | Scaffolds a [portal](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/getting-started/quickstart/) in `dir` (default: the current folder), using the OpenAPI files already there. |
| `dev [dir]` | Starts the dev server with live reload on `http://localhost:4321`. |
| `build [dir]` | Builds the static portal into `dist/`. |
| `serve [dist]` | Serves a built portal, with sign-in and access rules ([rapidoc serve](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/deploy/rapidoc-serve/)). Default folder `dist`. |
| `preview <spec>` | Shows one spec (a file or URL) in `<rapi-doc>` on `http://localhost:4000`, reloading when a file in its folder changes ([preview](/docs/cli/preview/)). |
| `mock [dir \| spec...]` | Mock server for a portal's APIs, a folder of specs, or spec files (paths or URLs), each under `/<api id>` ([Mock Server](https://mock.rapidocui.com/)). |
| `validate [spec \| dir]` | Validates one OpenAPI spec (a file or URL), or every OpenAPI spec and Arazzo spec in a portal ([validate](/docs/cli/validate/)). |
| `lint [spec \| dir]` | Checks what a spec needs to make a good portal: operationIds, summaries, examples, security, declared tags ([lint](/docs/cli/lint/)). |
| `bundle <spec>` | Writes a spec split over several files as one: other-file `$ref`s become components ([bundle](/docs/cli/bundle/)). |
| `pdf <spec>` | Writes the API reference of a spec as a PDF ([pdf](/docs/cli/pdf/)). Needs `rapipdf`. |
| `mcp export <spec>` | Writes an MCP server project for the spec ([mcp](/docs/cli/mcp/)). |
| `mcp serve <spec>` | Runs that MCP server over stdio, without writing files. |
| `migrate [--from <src>]` | Writes `rapidoc.config.yaml` from a `zudoku` or `redocly` project (found in the folder when `--from` is left out; [Migrating](https://portal.rapidocui.com/docs/tools/migrate/)). |
| `doctor [dir]` | Checks Node, the packages' versions, the portal config and the browser bundle; `--format json` for bug reports. |
| `completion <zsh \| bash \| fish>` | Prints a completion script for the shell ([Shell completion](#shell-completion)). |
| `help [command]` | Shows help, or one command's options and examples (same as `rapidoc <command> --help`). |
| `--version`, `-v` | Shows the version. |

Options and arguments can come in any order (`rapidoc build --out-dir public ./portal`). A misspelled command or option is an error with a suggestion (`Unknown option --outdir. Did you mean --out-dir?`).

## Options

| Option | Commands | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `--out-dir <path>` | build | Output folder. Default `dist`. |
| `--port <number>` | dev, serve, mock, preview | dev: default `4321`; serve: `$PORT` or `8080`; mock: `4010`; preview: `4000`. |
| `--host <host>` | serve, mock, preview | Address to listen on. Default `$HOST` (serve), `localhost` (preview), else `0.0.0.0`. |
| `--open` | dev, preview | Open the page in the browser. |
| `--theme <name>` | preview | `<rapi-doc>` theme. |
| `--mount-path <path>` | serve | Path requests arrive under, when a proxy strips part of the portal's path. Default `$RAPIDOC_MOUNT_PATH`, else the path of `site.url`. |
| `--issuer <url>` | mock | OpenID Connect issuer whose tokens are accepted. Default `$RAPIDOC_MOCK_ISSUER`. |
| `--audience <id>` | mock | Audience tokens must be issued for. Default `$RAPIDOC_MOCK_AUDIENCE`. |
| `--seed <number>` | mock | Seed for generated data. Default `1`. |
| `--mock-config <file>` | mock, lint | With `--stateful`: your corrections to what the mock worked out. Default: `mock.config.yaml` beside the spec. |
| `--delay <ms>` | mock | Wait this long before every API response, to see loading states in a client. Default `0`. |
| `--stream-interval <ms>` | mock | Gap between the items of a streamed response (OpenAPI 3.2 `itemSchema`). Default `300`. |
| `--stateful` | mock | Keep state: creates, updates and deletes change stored records that reads and lists return, seeded from the spec. |
| `--rows <number>` | mock | With `--stateful`: seed records per resource. Default `10`. |
| `--debug` | dev, build | Keep the temporary build workspace and print its path. |
| `--title <title>` | init | Site title. |
| `--spec <file>` | init | An OpenAPI file to include; repeat for more. Default: every one found in the folder. |
| `--starter-spec` | init | Use the starter spec instead of the OpenAPI files found. |
| `--force`, `-f` | init | Overwrite existing files (in a terminal, lists them and asks first). |
| `--no-install` | init | Skip `npm install`. |
| `--format <format>` | validate, lint, doctor, bundle | validate, lint, doctor: `pretty` (default), `json`, or `sarif` (validate, lint). bundle: `yaml` or `json` (default: by the output file's extension). |
| `--strict` | validate, lint | Fail on warnings too. |
| `--rule <name>=<severity>` | lint | A rule's severity: `error`, `warn` or `off`; repeatable. |
| `--rules` | lint | List the rules and their defaults. |
| `--stateful` | lint | Also report what the stateful mock had to assume or could not map. |
| `--remote` | validate, lint, mcp, bundle | Also fetch remote specs and remote `$ref`s. |
| `--output <file>`, `-o` | bundle, pdf | bundle: write here instead of stdout. pdf: default the spec's name with `.pdf`. |
| `--dereference` | bundle | Inline every `$ref`, in-file ones too. |
| `--no-validate` | bundle | Don't check the result against the OpenAPI Specification. |
| `--api <id>` | bundle, pdf | The spec of this API from `rapidoc.config.*`, instead of a file. |
| `--title <text>`, `--footer <text>` | pdf | Cover title (default `API Reference`) and page footer. |
| `--schema-style <style>` | pdf | `object` (default) or `table`. |
| `--examples`, `--api-list` | pdf | Add request and response examples; add a closing list of every operation. |
| `--no-info`, `--no-toc`, `--no-security`, `--no-api-details`, `--no-sort-tags` | pdf | Leave out the cover, the table of contents, the security schemes or the operations; keep the tags in the spec's order. |
| `--primary-color <color>`, `--alternate-color <color>` | pdf | The PDF's two colors (default `#b44646`, `#005b96`). |
| `--labels <file>`, `--font <file>`, `--mono-font <file>` | pdf | Labels to replace (JSON), and fonts in place of Roboto and Roboto Mono. |
| `--out-dir <path>` | mcp export | Where to write the project. Default `mcp-server`. |
| `--force`, `-f` | mcp export | Write into a folder that isn't empty. |
| `--arazzo <file>` | mcp | An Arazzo spec whose workflows become tools too. |
| `--server-name <name>` | mcp | The MCP server's name. Default: from the API title. |
| `--base-url <url>` | mcp serve | Call the API here instead of the spec's server (for example `rapidoc mock`). |
| `--help`, `-h` | all | Show the command's help instead of running it. |
| `--quiet`, `-q` | all | Print errors and warnings only. |
| `--yes`, `-y` | all | Don't ask anything: take the default answer to every question. |

## Questions

In a terminal, commands ask for what their options don't say, and `rapidoc` alone shows a menu of the common commands. When the output is piped, `CI` is set, or `--yes` is given, they never ask: they use the defaults, or stop and name the option to pass. Every question has an option, so any run can be scripted.

| Command | Asks | Option that answers it |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `init` | The site title, which of the OpenAPI files found to include, whether to run `npm install`. Then prints the command that does the same without questions. | `--title`, `--spec` / `--starter-spec`, `--no-install` |
| `init --force` | Whether to replace the existing files it lists. | `--yes` |
| `migrate` | Which project to migrate, when `--from` is left out (it looks for `redocly.yaml` and `zudoku.config.*`); whether to replace an existing `rapidoc.config.yaml`. | `--from`, `--yes` |
| `dev`, `serve`, `mock` | Whether to use the next free port when the port is taken. Without a terminal, `serve` and `mock` stop (`dev` moves to a free port by itself). | `--port`, `--yes` |

`Ctrl+C` on a question cancels the command (exit code `130`).

## Output and exit codes

On a terminal the CLI prints icons; when its output is piped or `NO_COLOR` is set, it prints plain text, with `error:` and `warning:` in front of problems. Errors and warnings go to stderr, everything else to stdout.

| Exit code | Means |
| :--- | :--- |
| `0` | Success. |
| `1` | A problem in the input: an invalid spec or config, a failed build, a missing package. |
| `2` | A wrong command line: an unknown command or option, a missing or malformed value. |
| `130` | Cancelled at a question (`Ctrl+C`). |

## Which packages each command needs

The CLI loads the other packages only when a command needs them:

| Command | Needs |
| :--- | :--- |
| `init`, `validate <spec>`, `lint <spec>` | `@rapidoc/cli` only |
| `dev`, `build`, `migrate`, `validate` and `lint` of a portal folder | `@rapidoc/portal` |
| `serve` | `@rapidoc/server` |
| `mock` | `@rapidoc/mock` (and `@rapidoc/portal` for a portal folder) |
| `preview`, `bundle <spec>`, `mcp export`, `doctor` | `@rapidoc/cli` only |
| `pdf` | `rapipdf` (and `@rapidoc/portal` with `--api`) |
| `bundle --api` | `@rapidoc/portal` |
| `mcp serve` | `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` |

## Shell completion

`rapidoc completion <shell>` prints a script that completes commands, options, their values (`--format pretty|json|sarif`, `mcp export|serve`) and file names. It is generated from the commands themselves, so it matches the installed version; regenerate it after updating.

```bash
# zsh: a folder in $fpath, before compinit runs (or: eval "$(rapidoc completion zsh)" in ~/.zshrc)
rapidoc completion zsh > ~/.zsh/completions/_rapidoc
```

```bash
# bash: in ~/.bashrc
eval "$(rapidoc completion bash)"
```

```bash
# fish
rapidoc completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/rapidoc.fish
```

With `npx` instead of a global install, use `npx rapidoc completion zsh` once to write the file; `eval` on every shell start would run npx each time.

## Examples

```bash
rapidoc init my-portal --title "Acme Developer Portal"
rapidoc dev
rapidoc build ./my-api-portal
rapidoc serve dist --port 8080
rapidoc mock --issuer https://example.us.auth0.com/ --audience https://api.example.com
rapidoc mock ./specs --port 4011
rapidoc validate ./specs/orders-api.yaml
rapidoc lint --strict
rapidoc bundle ./specs/orders-api.yaml -o dist/orders-api.json
rapidoc migrate --from zudoku
```

Source: https://rapidocui.com/docs/cli/reference/
